title: Eric DeCosta's Post-Draft Press Conference | Baltimore Ravens
text: weekend. It was a long uh three days, a lot of work involved. Uh happy with the results. Um I'll just kind of run down these guys that we've taken the most recent picks. Uh Elijah Sarat from Indiana. U St. Francis Grat as you guys know. Uh great career at Indiana. Big body, strong hands. Um contested catch. Probably a guy that can play outside or inside. We think he's really really good inside. Um really a good back shoulder fade type of receiver, physical, you know, just we just think he's a really good fit for what we want to do on offensively and was, you know, I think speaks to us trying to draft best available player whenever we can and he just was really at that point in the draft. We had some other options, but in our mind he was clearly the best player still available. Um Hibner, uh we've seen him here in Baltimore. Um he was a local local guy for us, local proday guy um from Virginia. Uh Jesse knew him from his Michigan days. Uh really think he's he's he's really evolved uh tested really really well at the combine. His numbers are off the charts. Uh really really explosive, a great jumper, really good ball skills. Uh had an awesome year as a receiving tight end. We think he's going to emerge as a blocker as well. A great kid. Uh we love spending time with him here in Baltimore. Uh Chandler Rivers was a guy that I I know the scouts are really excited to get. Undersized, very very quick, probably fits best inside. He plays outside, but probably fits best inside. Uh very sticky in coverage. Again, a guy that tested extremely well. Um his his numbers at the combine is 40. I think was in the four threes. He jumped really well. Um and we've had, you know, success over the years with these type of guys. even going back to, you know, some of my favorite Ravens Darius Webb is a guy that comes to mind. Taon Young, those those kind of really good football players that might be a little unders sized. Um, so we're excited about him. Uh, and then Josh Quavvis, uh, you know, you never can go wrong with an Alabama tight end. Uh, he's a guy that does a lot of different things well. He runs good routes. He's got good hands. He's a competitive blocker. Uh, he can align in different spots. And I think one of our goals this year was really coming out of this draft with with two tight ends that that we liked a lot. And um you know, I think we did a good job. I really credit uh our coaches, Zach and and uh Declan, for really doing a great job getting that tight end board lined up in a really nice way for us to strategize and make sure that we got a couple guys that we really liked. and they weren't necessarily, you know, players that we had to jump into the, you know, first or second or third round to get, but we had options in every single round. And, uh, and we were very fortunate to get Josh at that point. Uh, Adam Randle's an interesting pick. I think it is. You'll probably see the video at some point. It's the first draft pick that Steve Bashad has ever made. So, uh, you know, when we were down in Florida, Steve was begging for a draft pick and he owns the team. I said, "Yes, Steve." And so, um, of course, you're gonna have a draft pick. And so, we decided on our last fifth round pick. Uh, he did his research. Um, he studied the tape, talked to people. Um, he's he's got a really good relationship with the Clemson head coach. Um, and Adam's a guy as a former wide out. He's got a varied skill set. He does a lot of different things well. Uh, we think the best is yet to come with him as a running back. He's got really good hands. He can run routes. He's a possible kick returner, special teams guy. He's got a great body and good measurables and we're excited to see what he can do. He's kind of a jack knife. Uh and he's a phenomenal kid. We think uh one of the one of the best makeups in this draft. Um and then Ryan Eckley. Uh you know, Randy has been scouring the country looking at punters and this was his top guy. And I think for us it was just a matter of when we had to take them. Looking at the board, kind of getting a sense for the teams that might draft the punter. We knew Buffalo was in the mix and potentially Pittsburgh. Uh so we had to figure out that sweet spot to get that done. And uh the nice thing I think about, you know, Ryan is not only is he an excellent punter, but he's probably the best holder in the draft, which is really important, uh as you guys all know. So excited to get him. Rashan Benny, um you know, we we've actually we've coached him, right? Lu Espazito and Jesse. Uh we like his his frame, his skill set. He's a guy that can play five-tech, three-tech, physical guy, long arms, really has a good five-tech body, which is tough to find. He's a strong run defender. Uh, and he fits us. He fits our mentality, and he knows our defense, and he's a he's a plug-and-play guy coming in right out of the gates. Now, last pick is Evan Bernstein. Uh, again, a guy that plays guard. He has played some center, not a lot. Uh, he's he's been playing college football for a long time. And uh he was at I think uh South Dakota and then Northwestern. Uh he's a guard primarily physical, tough, gritty type of Midwest, Big 10 type of offensive lineman. And at that point in the draft, he was by far the highest rated player for us and we think he's got a good chance to help us at some point. Questions? So Eric, when you're when Steve's making that, why did you select that that fifth round as the the one that you know, was there any kind of any backstory to why that was the the the point in the draft that he was going to take one? >> I think he just he probably uh coerced me with a nice bottle of wine down there in Florida and we had all those picks. We knew we were going to have all those picks and so we just decided on that that last pick in the fifth round. Um, obviously maybe your best offseason departure is Kevin Linder Balm. Um, no obvious center in this draft, although I guess, you know, Evan might convert. Um, what was your overall take on this center class available in this draft and ultimately, you know, you even traded back into the fourth round uh when there were some available. Why did do you think it wasn't in your best interest to take one? >> Yeah, I mean, I think it's a good question. Um, so there were a couple centers that we really liked. Um, the guys that went in the second round. And I think after that, you know, could we have traded up, you know, potentially maybe traded up into the second round and maybe take one of those guys? And we we really assessed it like where we were picking at 80 for us to do that would have cost our second round pick, our third round pick and our fourth round pick points wise to do that. Um, but know third round, fourth round, fifth round, whatever you're going to say pointswise to do it. probably prohibitive for us to get up that high in the draft. And so, you know, um would I rather have Jacobe, uh Serat, and uh and and and Hibner? I probably would than one player at that point. So, it was impossible for us to really get back up into the second round unless we gave up a first round pick next year, maybe potentially. Um, you know, there were some other centers, but there was nobody that we looked at that we thought necessarily like this guy's going to come in here and, you know, I'm not good players, but there's nobody that's going to necessarily be an impact player for us this year. Um, I do think we'll have a plan um at the position. Feel confident in saying that. And I think we have a couple guys here that will compete for that position. But um as the uh a hall of fame general manager once said um you don't play games till September and I think we'll have a great offensive line at that point. We have a plan. Uh it didn't necessarily fall our way this weekend, but it's still early and I'm thrilled with what we'll be able to accomplish. Derek, were you surprised that the two guys win as early as they did? Those first two centers. >> I was uh I was a little surprised. Um I would probably attribute that to the run on offensive linemen in the first and second round and that trickle down effect. Um because uh you know, you saw those tackles and guards go um you know that's what happens. I I think you see it you saw it in a different way this year with receiver and tight ends. And so again, you saw these receivers get picked and then you saw a huge run on tight ends. Um these teams have to adjust quickly on the fly. So, um I think actually one of the one of the centers that was drafted got turned in as a guard. Um just because all those guards got picked and so now as a team you're trying to look at it and go, "Oh man, how are we going to fill this guard position? Well, let's take this center. He can probably play guard." So it's hard. It's challenging. Um, a lot of times when you find yourself in a position like that, and we've been in this many years, is it's just the pick that you have, the number that you have, um, and not just being able to maneuver, uh, the right way or not not having the ammunition, um, or maybe the the cost of doing so is probably prohibitive. So, unfortunate, but I'm ecstatic with the players that we're able to get. And um honestly like looking at this list of players, I probably wouldn't do anything differently. >> For for you or for Jesse, what what is your guys plan now with Emry? Is someone Is he someone who you're still looking at at guard or a tackle or is he someone who could even potentially have a shot at center? >> Yeah. Well, I mean, coming out, he was a right tackle and he's a damn good right tackle. Um we think he's going to be a damn good guard, too. um coming off the injury. We think he's a talented guy, great mentality, great makeup. Um and you know, he's going to compete. He'll compete to start and we're going to have great depth and we're going to have a great six-man. I don't know who that sixman's going to be, but whoever it is, if you come out of it in with this group, you're going to be really talented. You're going to be really good. So, I like the depth that we have right now. We still have some moves to make. I think we're in a much better place than we have been. Um, and I'm excited to see what happens. >> Jesse, I know you were kind of non-committal in terms of venue where he would play, but I mean, does he have that? I knew he played a little bit of center. That's something you guys would even look at. >> Yeah, I think we'll start off thinking more of a guard, but I think there's always I I really think coach Leadford does a great job. Um, highly confident that we'll be able to put a great O line together. I do think there will be a there's the thought of how do you get your best five guys on the field, you know, no different than a guy like secondary or, you know, linebackers. It's like how do you how do you get the best players that can help you win onto the field and so I think that's the great part about the offseason getting a chance to work with these guys. It's a it's a good time sometimes to experiment with with people like that and see what see the versatility that guys have. Uh and then again come September, you know, figure out figure out where where everybody fits best, where they can best thrive and succeed and uh help us have the best O line. >> Jesse, um Eric mentioned yesterday three guys. I mean, Z Pinter, Vaughn, and um >> are those the three guys you talked about? >> Yeah, those three guys for sure. I think uh we feel good about those guys competing. Um, and then again, just like all the guys, all the interior, all the offensive linemen, having that ability to potentially, you know, showcase some versatility and play different spots and and us figure out the best five, the best six, the best seven, the best eight, you know, that'll be a major work in progress between now and September. >> Jesse, when you sort of step back and look at the 11 guys you drafted over the last three days, do you see any sort of theme that runs through the entire class? um you know, tough, physical, you know, a lot of those these guys are big physical players. Um when you look at when you look at the O line, obviously you start with Venga and just like him setting the tone for the draft class. Um dominant line of scrimmage and so think we added, you know, the best interior interior offensive lineman in the draft. Um Zion again, big physical, tough, rugged player. Jacobe, big matchup guy. Size, speed, length, catch radius, ability to make tough plays. Um, I mean, Srod as well, like that was a really cool opportunity to double dip at that position. The way the board fell and taking the best guy, a guy that's had a ton of production in major impact games the last two years at Indiana. And then I I think when guys are really productive wherever they're playing, you know, he played a year at a JMU, he played a year at even a smaller school before that. A super productive player. U Hibner, you know, I mean, I've seen this guy in some really bloody physical nine on sevens, you know, two, three, four years ago. Um being a really physical blocker, even maybe more so than showed up in and what they were asking him to do at SMU. Uh again, excited about him. Uh, but all the guys, I mean, you you can go all the way down the list. Even Chandler Rivers, not as big in in stature, but plays with a really cool mindset. Love the way that guy plays football. Attacks the ball, plays really physical. He's a good tackler for his size. Um, so I just think you go all the way down the list. Um, it's a really physical group. Big, big, strong, tough, physical team that we're trying to trying to have here. And all these guys fit that bill. Jesse, um it's been probably a blur these couple months of everything you've had on your plate. What was this experience like in your new role with all the first you're experiencing? And what's kind of a general takeaway for you just being part of your first draft as a head coach? >> Yeah, it was incredible. Uh you know, this is the this is the obviously we talked about this all the way back, but like this is the job I wanted because the people here and how they operate and Eric does an amazing job. Uh you got Azie Newsome sitting in there. You got Steve Bashadotti. Just people that are unbelievable. Uh you know, people first and then they they can just manage situations. They got a great mind for what's happening throughout the draft. They've done a great job of bringing the coaches in. And I feel like everybody on the staff really felt value and felt input into how we ended up with these players, you know, which I think is a cool quality to have to to make to bring people in and make it make it collaborative. Um, but at the end of the day, man, it's just a cool, really cool situation to kind of see the team come together. Um, you know, when you go into it, there's, I think, you know, 50 so players on our team and you add 11 and then obviously we'll add more the rest of the day. It'll be really exciting when we look out there and there's uh 90 guys on the roster. >> What was there a position that Eric kind of tasked you with evaluating specific prospect class? >> You know, it was really cool. I I've always taken really a lot of pride as an evaluator. Um it was it was honestly really neat and fun to to do a lot of different positions um over the time and so first time really evaluating like offensive linemen and wide receivers in a way in a different way than just preparing to play against them. Um, you know, and and and to me, like the things that jump out as a as a defensive history coach, I would say, you know, the play style and how these guys play and just like the down after down mindset that they play with when you're looking at offensive players really jumps off the tape with all these guys. Their ability to make tough, especially like the the playmakers, the skilled players, their ability to make tough plays, contested plays, key plays on the field in the red area. both these guys, both these wide receivers, huge red zone uh targets. So, just fun to evaluate all the different positions and look at different things. Um, and then certainly, you know, the secondary has probably always been a knack of mine to try to get some of those guys. >> Eric, uh, obviously you have very detailed records of of all these guys and their various idiosyncrasies, but, you know, you look at your two receivers in in Jacobe and Elijah and then your two tight ends. Um, you know, very sort of similar on the surface profiles for each of those positions. I mean, high point, you know, tall receivers and tight ends or maybe sort of tweener types who have blocking ability and then some, you know, pass catching. >> Are there ways in which those guys sort of diverge from each other or is the overlap some of the point and why you decided to draft them? Yeah, I think the the biggest thing I think is just that we they're they're versatile players that do some really good things. Um they're not exactly the same. You know, our vision for Jacobe is probably a little bit different than maybe the vision for Sarat. They're going to compete for playing time, right? They both catch the ball really well. They're both big. Um but they're not exactly identical. I think u you know Matt and Josh um they're a little different. They're a little different how they're used and the offense is different, but I love the fact that they're both versatile players who can do different things. And in our offense, not to not to give a lot away, and I don't even understand our offense yet to be honest, but I know that versatility and flexibility and being able to do a lot of different things is really important. Being smart, being adaptable, um is really, really important. The idea of deception and all these things and just flexibility to play multiple roles, I think, is really a plus. And so, um, you know, and then just being able to handle the physical aspect of the game, being tough, being tough minded, being able to handle adversity, um, you know, uh, again, like I talked a little bit yesterday about this, but I had a bunch of other players reach out to me today um about some of these guys and just they know their stories and I think these guys were made, you know, of the right stuff, most of these guys and I want to thank for that. I just think it's opportunity for me to thank the scouts specifically um the area guys and then also um couple unheralded guys um Steve Claget and Derek Yam as well. They do a lot of work on the draft in different ways um George and Mark and all those guys and and Nick. But we get great information on how these guys kind of who they are as people, background, motivations, drivers and all those different things. and the scouts and and those guys upstairs, they're really the guys that are able to kind of put that all together for me to help me make the decisions. And so without that, this process would be much more complicated and probably not as not as accurate. So >> sort of on the topic of versatility, um you know, Declan comes from the Shawn Payeyton school and Shawn's offense. Think of Taesm Hill as sort of a do it all jack knife type guy. I think you use the word jack knife when describing Adam. um you know as a receiver turned running back. I mean is there sort of a Joker jack knife role or that he could kind of be in the running for that's new to this offense? >> Well I think that remains to be seen but I will say he's very smart. He's big. He's athletic. He catches the ball well. He runs good routes. He's physical. He's a physical runner. He's played special teams. He can return kicks. So his value it does get it does get magnified. And I think uh not not to speak for coach, but one of the hardest things to do is is come up with a 48man roster and uh if you have guys who can do multiple things, it really makes your job a lot easier because now you can you can you can create roles for other people because you might have a player who can do more than just one thing. So if you can run routes, run the ball, pass, protect, and return kicks, now your value really skyrockets. Eric, I know you were uh dialed in to the whole draft, but did you get a chuckle out of watching uh Mark Ingram's son or the lady from uh the UK? >> We did. We laughed. We saw that, you know. Um yeah, it was it was great. I mean, Mark, you know, he's I think someone said it, but you know, you'd think that Mark spent his whole career with us. He's only with us two years, but they were memorable years and that 19 season especially, he's got a special place in my heart and I think of him as a as a real original Raven, even though obviously he played more more years in New Orleans. And so guy that I really respect, I love his passion. I thought was really funny. Um, and you know, certainly I think the uh back and forth between, you know, Pittsburgh and Baltimore, we we saw that this weekend, right? And I think that's is kind of actually a special thing, right? It's kind of fun that we have that type of rivalry that's like celebrated across the country. Everybody understands like what it's like Red Sox, Yankees, you know. Um, everybody understands it and kind of celebrates it. I think it's one of the things that makes sports special. >> How's the scouting process compared to find equally this year after you're looking for a kicker last year in the pre-draft? >> Oh man. Well, I don't get involved in that too much, you know. Um, and I'm not I don't want to, you know, I don't want to create a monster, but he's already been created, you know, he's already been created. Uh, but Randy does a phenomenal job. He does. And so, um, it's probably the one the two positions that if Randy comes to me and says, "This is the guy that we need," I'm going to accept it. Normally I'd be like a little skeptical and I want to watch the tape and do my homework and put my eyes on the guy, but when Randy does this and says, "Yeah, this is the best one." Then that resonates and um you know, I think our track record with kickers and pawners is pretty good. Long snappers is pretty good. Um so it's not something I'm going to mess with. So, um, now I might fight with him as to when we have to draft the guy or what round, but as far as like being the best at ranking, I think he's the best at that. >> Do you look at Monday, I guess Monday at 4 after that, um, free agent signings no longer counter the comp formula. You're fond of saying that building a roster is sort of an everyday thing year round. Do you view this almost as another phase of free agency for this team? We do. Um yeah, I mean, you know, we don't have any agreements that would be illegal, of course. Um but there's always there always players out there that you can go after that you'll try to talk to at some point. And as you the draft is really, you know, you kind of you you go through this process and now you know what the roster looks like. So now it's easy next week to go out and say, "Okay, we need this, we might need this, we might need this." Um, so I think with free agency, potentially trades, um, terminated players, you know, we still June 1st still at risk for players to be terminated. There were opportunity for us to sign a few guys. And as you guys know, like even I remember, you know, I think uh I don't know what year that was, but 2021, maybe 22, I was at driving up to Penn State with my daughter and we signed uh I negotiated the contract for Javian Clowney in the car. That was in August. So I think it was in August, right? It was in August. Yeah. So those things can happen, right? And so again, it's like we try to be patient, not be uh too reactive to things, not overreact, just to be patient, and we'll see what happens. Let good players fall to us. There's going to be opportunities coming along, and we'll be ready to pounce. Jesse, >> how have you seen Raan Benny progress both when you were with him in Michigan and since then? >> Yeah, Ray's a u tough, rugged, physical defensive lineman that's got some real athleticism. I think there's some real upside there with him and some pass rush ability. Uh he got thought in 2023 he was our third or fourth type defensive lineman. We had Mason and Kenneth Grant and Chris Jenkins and we had obviously a pretty loaded group. Um but he made some really key plays for us in that season. He got hurt in the Rose Bowl that year. Um and it I know it affected him. I was gone after that. But I thought this year he really bounced back after kind of battling through the injury in 2024. Showed some really good stuff. does a lot of things on tape that that obviously we like to see. Um, and so I think he's just kind of a guy that's gotten better and better. He was really really raw and kind of a young player coming into Michigan. Um, but uh those guys there, you know, I know he's been well trained and and well coached and uh excited to add Ray. >> Jesse, we didn't get a chance to ask you about your voluntary mini camp you were able to have this past week. what stood out about that in terms of you know guys attendance and just what did you learn about your football team getting to have most of them together for the first time? >> Yeah, I mean it was unbelievable turnout. Uh we had a great three days together. I think we learned a lot about each other just kind of how we're operating on the practice field. some of the things that we're doing. We didn't do a ton of full speed team work in that just from a health and safety standpoint of where we're at in the offseason program, but the guys had a real opportunity to kind of see where they're at learning the learning new schemes on both sides of the ball. Um, and so it was it was incredible. It was a lot of fun. Um, it was cool to see the coaches out there coaching these guys up. We kind of knew it kind of gives you a especially going into the draft, it gives you a little bit of sense at different positions and kind of where you're at. Um, and so it's a it's a great rule. I do I do love that for new staffs to be able to have that opportunity. And uh now we go right back into phase two and uh continue to try to get better. >> Eric, um since we're not actually talk to you until September now, uh any anything you can tell us about uh progress with Lamar and contract talks? >> No, not really. Okay. Thank you.

title: HC Kevin Stefanski & GM Ian Cunningham Day Three Press Conference | 2026 NFL Draft | Atlanta Falcons
text: All right. Um, everybody's in the same spots except Will. Um, good seeing everybody. Feel like we came out of this day with uh some good football players, guys that are going to be able to help us. Um, we're excited about It was uh fun in the draft room this morning. We had the scouts come in and and give their players that they were passionate about that were still left on the board. It was good to kind of hear them speak with some conviction uh in the morning. and then uh some some of them during the draft as well. So, it's always fun day three of the draft just to be able to get some players that we all are excited about and uh look forward to them contributing uh to our organization. So, uh with that we'll open it up. >> Kevin Ory and where do you think like Perkins will be playing mostly defensively? >> Yeah, work through it. He's obviously had the ability to play off and on the ball. uh you know, somebody that like Ian was mentioning, you you had good players this roster as coaches. Uh that's our job to find their roles based on what they've done on tape and also explore some things that maybe they haven't done. Uh you know, in particular in this case, obviously uh it's it's some versatility along the front, but also there's uh you know, excited about the special teams component of that as well. And you talked about um wanting to add depth and um I'm sure you were hoping to get a fifth runner, but uh how did you feel about the way that worked out to to trade him to get to get a six? >> Yeah, it felt like it worked out well. We were able to get another player uh with the trade. Um you know, we had some other calls uh that were kind of going on and then at the end of the day we decided to trade back with Vegas and uh uh yeah, it worked out well that we were able to get another player. kind of a similar question about about Kendall Daniels. Um feels like an older guy as far as you know his size and that position. What's the vision for for him at linebacker? >> Good. Yeah, with Kendall just coming from Oklahoma State as a former safety. Uh to your point, yeah, he's a he's definitely a brick guy, fits those measurables and what he looks for and what we look for. and um then going to OU and playing in the venable scheme and you see him play all over the field stacked and the apex and sometimes even the line deep. So he's a rare athlete, you know, uh when you watch the tape, the movement, the the length, the fluidity. Uh he can do a lot of things for you uh on defense. I know Barrett and and Brick and obviously Kevin, the whole coaching staff were all excited that we were able to get him where we did. Deion Burks had a kind of a strange fall in this draft. He was just taken, I guess, in the end of the seventh round. But was there like a medical thing or or or what what did you guys see your evaluation of Burks? >> Yeah. Um I don't I don't I don't know. I don't know. I didn't even know he got drafted. Sorry, >> Ian. This process as a whole, this this three days or whatever you think, how did it go, you know, for you? Did it go sort of like you thought? Did it all fit together like you imagined it would? >> Yeah, it feel like it we uh we got some good players. We got, you know, some good players that are going to be able to help our football team offensively and defensively. It was a great experience. It felt like the the crew upstairs. We got to give a lot of credit to to the guys and the girls upstairs that that helped get this thing um organized and and it ran smooth. Uh we've got a lot of support, a lot of people up there put a lot of countless hours um not just in you know the scouts and the coaches but the whole operation. So uh really a lot of the credit goes to them. >> When you're like in the later rounds is it as simple as you know here's our top rated player, let's get him or is it is there a debate about let's talk about these five guys or what what does that look like? >> Yeah it um I'd say a little bit of both. Uh there are times where you know like there's a a guy that you're targeting. Sometimes you may want to try to trade up for that guy. I think you've you know have heard us talk about you know those positional cliffs or um you know best player available and you sometimes you try to make an effort to go up and get some guys. Um it doesn't work out sometimes and then sometimes they just fall in your lap, right? So it's case by case and I think at the end of the draft you're really just looking for players that are uh the best fits that fits us. Obviously throughout the draft, you're looking for guys that fit you culturally, but the best fit and uh the best value at that point. >> Were you guys surprised that uh that Perkins fell as far as he is? A few years ago, he was, >> you know, probably graded as a first round guy. >> Yeah, we we're happy to get him in. Um you know, you see you see what he's able to do um all over the field. Early in his career, playing off the edge and rushing the passer and like you mentioned, you thought this was going to be the next one. and unfortunately, you know, he's had he's battled some injuries earlier in his career and he's come back. Um, and we're excited about the versatility that he brings and uh excited about where we got him. >> How do you weigh a player like him? Like would you guys watch him like pre-injury, after the injury, like how how far back are you guys like watching him? You >> know, we've got scouts that have gone into the schools every single year. So, I remember some of the conversations about um about Harold were uh from some of the scouts that went in, they talked about his freshman year, right? And they talked about how he jumped off the tape and what he looked like and uh thinking that we were going to be able to get him to that form with our coaching staff um if we were to be able to draft him. So, you do watch a little bit of before and after and and maybe just try to see, you know, one of the reasons why he uh you know, maybe not what he was back then. and maybe because of the injury, right? Or maybe because of development or he's playing in a different position. So, you kind of try to weigh a lot of a lot of those things. >> And does it make it um easier to with a guy like Daniels with with Perkins to kind of bet on the development of their traits, even if you maybe the college production wasn't there, when you've got a coach like Jeff who has a history of developing these players and and kind of making them into good pros. >> Definitely. title: That's a Wrap! GM Monti Ossenfort & Asst. GM Dave Sears Talk NFL Draft | 2026 Arizona Cardinals
text: Got Dave tonight. Good to see you guys. All right, so sorry we just just finished up the seventh round. Obviously you see the guys are upstairs kind of finishing up the undrafted process kind of grinding through that. You know, we'll add a few guys there not going to be a huge class of undrafted guys but we'll have a few of those guys that we hopefully get locked up here in the next half hour so day started took Caleb Proctor out of defensive tackle out of Southeast Louisiana. You know, kind of came on through the process had a good really good season this year really productive season saw him down at the East West game and then continued a strong spring process worked out well both at the combine and his pro day and then we had him in here on a 30 visit enjoyed our time with him there. And then Reggie Virgil you know, had a good year this year Texas Tech had a good season another guy that we had and enjoyed a big personality on Reggie and entertaining guy had him in here on a 30 visit as well six round Carson Sherar linebacker out of University of Iowa. Sorry I got a little allergy thing going on here. You know, productive player for Iowa this year had been a productive special teams player his whole career. You know, excited what he can do for us defensively in the kicking game and then finished up at the top of the seventh round with Jaden Williams offensive tackle from from Ole Miss. So no movement no trades. You know, had a couple opportunities nothing quite got us excited to to move out on anything. That's way it goes sometimes but you know, excited about the the seven guys we added at the in the undrafted group. We'll see how that all shakes out but you know, I think we added some some guys are going to help out our our team and increase the competition throughout all levels of the team. So let it let you guys fire them at us. Dave with with a guy like Caleb how do you kind of go about measuring what he can be compared to maybe some of the opposition he might have played out. I mean you're watching the game tape but there's there's got to be some projection right? Yeah, I mean the the good thing is he played it against LSU this year. Obviously that's the tape that everybody's going to go to but he did play against other schools in the past. You know, FBS schools stuff like that and then you have men in All Star game so you get to watch it for multiple practices against bigger school cop. It's a case where the kid succeeded in each one of those opportunities and he's also been able to stack weight. I think it is pro day he was up into the 290s. You know, so still tested very well. So you're seeing some growth potential as well as being able to compete when you put them on the same level some of those bigger school guys. It seemed like as you guys went through the day you guys ended up with a lot of players in this draft class that were high on that athleticism scale. Is that something you guys were looking at or is that just coincidence? I'd say more coincidence but you know, obviously like more athletic the better. Yeah, I've I've seen that I've seen that used. You know, you know, yeah, our guys tested high. That's that's good. That's good. I wouldn't say it's it's something that we necessarily target although you know, whenever we can add a good athlete that's always a positive. Are there certain positions where you see that is maybe more valuable than others to to have some of that elite level athleticism testing? Sure. I mean I think in every position whenever you know, but I also think you got to be you be careful. You know, there's guys that that test really well and score well on that and then maybe they put the pads on and they get on the field and that may not always translate. So you know, that's that's one metric. You know, I would say there there's plenty of plenty of examples of guys that that um test pot test highly on that type of stuff and then that doesn't translate to the field and the opposite there's guys that don't test well but hey when you turn on the tape, you know, wow this guy's a pretty good athlete. So it's a it's another piece. One of those examples of the last thing you were talking about Reggie was saying that you told him you were actually happy that he ran a 457 40 because he might have slipped down the board. What did he show you on tape because he's talking about how he can take the top off defenses. You don't think that when you see 457. What did he show you on tape that kind of made you feel like he has that skill set? Yeah, I think that's a great example. I mean you know, when you when you watch the tape of of Reggie he's played against high level of competition this season at Texas Tech and you know, they played made it into the playoffs and and played against good teams. I mean you don't turn on the tape and and say Reggie's slow. You know, so in the end that's what matters. Like there can be guys that run really fast and test really fast and then they don't show that on tape and you know, Reggie when you turn on the tape of Reggie he he does not play slow. So that's that's more important is what's on tape. With Caleb I I saw him listed anywhere between just right under 6'2 to 6'3. How will will his height translate to the NFL can impact what he can do here? Well, I mean it's really that's where he's going to have to improve his technique take the coaching. You know, you always hear low man wins and leverage and stuff like that. So if you have loose hips if you can sink and bend your knees and your ankles which Caleb can do it could be a an advantage to you but you have to have your hand placement correct. You have to have enough lower body strength all those kind of things. It's not like shorter is necessarily better but he's not to the point where he's so height deficient that he can't play a certain position or in a scheme. You know what I mean? And especially rushing the passer when you have bigger offensive lineman who might be a little stiffer trying to get down on you and you can sink and get around that can be an asset. You know what I mean? Obviously the draft board didn't necessarily fall to get an edge type player. Kind of where do you see the pass rush edge group for you right now as the roster stands? Yeah, I mean I think we got we got a lot of guys there that played a lot of ball between you know, Sweaty Baron Zaven you know, BJ BJ had a you know, tough year last year coming off the knee and you know, never really looked quite you know, all the way back. You know, Jordan Burch going into his second year. You know, so I think we have a group and then also Elliot Brown necko in that and that room as well. So you know, I think we have a group that is is a good mix of guys that have are experienced that played a lot. You know, and we got to find a way to put them in the best position. So obviously always going to look to add and and increase and and raise the talent level but just didn't work out that way to to add to that group and over the last three days. A lot of guys are coming from winning programs. How much stock do you put into that when you're doing the evaluation? I mean it's nice but I you know, I don't I don't know that that's necessarily a focal point. You know, but obviously you like guys that have been around winning. You like guys that you know, they're they're obviously coming from programs that are doing something right. So that's always good always good to see guys and then that's going to help them make that transition to a higher level of competition. So not necessarily a focal point but it's also a nice benefit. With Jaden I know he played both sides of the line. Is there a plan to start him out on one side or just kind of use that versatility to start off? Yeah, I mean he's he's played played you know, mainly right tackle but also saw quite a few snaps at left tackle as well in his career. I mean I think some 34 some starts in his career. So you know, another guy that you know, he's played against good competition in the SEC but also he's probably blocked as good of guys in practice like with the defensive line that they had coming out of there last year. He's he's saw good competition throughout his whole career. So you know, with the with that with the tackle position it's it's one that we work all our guys both sides and that will be no different for Jaden. Just going off that you bring back Elijah Wilkinson. Is that someone you see right now as a starting right tackle just given what you guys did in the draft and other moves? Yeah, I mean Elijah you know, Elijah started 16 games or something last year for Atlanta. So yeah, I think he'll certainly be in the mix. You know, not really naming starters anywhere right now but I think Elijah will definitely have a have a chance there. Elijah's another guy who he's played a lot of ball. He's played at different positions. He started you know, the first go around with us. He was inside at guard. He's also played a lot of tackle in his career. So like the versatility that he has but yeah, he'll definitely be in the mix at right tackle. Day three always seems to be a little bit more like volatile in terms of like the the player talent and the dark horses and you can find with all of these like later round guys to have them see the success they have in the NFL? No, I just think you know, we have a pretty good process. We put a lot of work into it. Him and I Rob Kissel spend a lot of hours up there watching the tape of later round guys. I don't think that's universal through everybody's draft process where the top level decision makers pour into the late rounds as much as they do the early rounds. We got a lot of good scouts who have conviction on some of these guys. We have an analytics department who helps guide us. You know, they got their systems all their different charts their bells are system whatever they use. But so we get a lot of input from a lot of people and we take it seriously. You know, as a lifetime scout I hate when people like ah it's just a six or seven who cares like really? I can name you a lot of good players who were found in those rounds who end up mattering for their team. So I think as long as you emphasize it you know, you should be able to do it pretty well. We talked to Montez about Carson playing in some high pressure games and moments. You have a number of guys who played in the playoff and then even Caleb's game at LSU is high pressure. You know, how do you as a scout kind of evaluate where do you put playing in big games big moments on your list of I guess intangibles and whatnot? Well, I think it's important like you know, clutch play you you could label it that but it's more so you know, you're looking for matchups too. Who's the guy playing against? It could be a big game and he's got a weak opponent and he goes off in that game but you know, it's really the matchups of Carson Beck's going against Texas A&M's defense or you know, Ohio State's defense things like that that you're looking at as much as what is the stage. You know what I mean? Along those lines I think you guys drafted three or four guys that played in the Shrine Bowl particularly. You had mentioned earlier about Proctor you get to see him against those guys like the ability to see those guys in those All Star games against guys that are going in the draft and maybe are a little bit higher than even if they played in a big conference because those are the best of the best. I mean, how important are the are those games and do you guys take a good chunk of what you're getting out when you go to these these all-star games? Yeah, I I mean, I think any exposure you get is important. The thing about all-star games is you get or your scouts get to go to these games and watch the guys consecutive practices in a row, which you don't really do at schools. You you might hit a school in August, hit it again in October, hit it again maybe late November or something, but they're watching guys practice boom boom boom. Uh so, they get a feel for like the competition. Some guys will improve over the course of this you know, hey, this guy's improving if he can do that, there's more there. And the other thing is like we have our coaches at these games. Chris Cook worked the East-West Shrine Game. He knows Jaden from that game. So, he can tell us, hey, the guy was really good in the meeting room. He learned here here's his technique that he picked up pretty quickly. I was teaching him or you know, vice versa. If it's negative impact, something like that. I clearly wasn't in that case, but uh so, that is um very valuable to us, but it's not necessarily any more important than any other one, but you you get a a good experience when you dial in on that stuff. Dave, with the Carson Shyre, he was talking about how much pride he takes in playing special teams. But in what ways can you see his linebacker instincts when you play special teams? Run ahead. I mean, that's the name of the game. Like you don't see the guy putting the brakes on before he runs through somebody's face and that's what special teams is, you know what I mean? So, uh linebacker obviously is a position where everybody leans on that position for special teams playing. When a guy has that background, like you usually know the guy's tough, you usually know he'll work hard, whether he can run or not, like all things that translate to defense eventually, you know. Marty, you said your undrafted class won't be very big. Why what what goes into that decision? Just really roster number, you know, our roster was at a point point where um we didn't have a ton of room. So, you know, it's it really comes down to that. I think we'll be six to eight uh somewhere in there. How do you say you approach a draft? You're very big on like best player available, but do you go into a draft thinking, hey, I want to accomplish this or want to maybe like satisfy this group? And if you did have any of those goals, did you accomplish them? Yeah, I mean, I think I think really the the the main goal of of any draft is just to improve the talent level and this is the biggest um roster building time of the year. These three days, you know, that's um you you know how many players you're going to be able to add and um there's no better no bigger time that you get to add this volume of players. And so, you know, I think we go in um you know, having a feel for what our roster having a feel for what it looks like, but in the end, all we want to do is add talent, add competition and just improve the the construction of our roster overall. Marty, you said throughout the off season that you want to kind of build the foundation for this team, but you also want to build a team that can compete in 2026. Where do you kind of feel like you're at you know, now that the primary roster building windows of the off season are done? Uh yeah, I mean, I like I I I'd I'd say the roster building never really ends, you know, it's a it's a constant evolving. Um you know, we won't get into too much competition this spring. There really is no competition, I should say. Um that the real competition won't start, but I mean, there's going to be players that come available next week that um you know, because of the draft, because of free or undrafted free agent signings, there's going to be another round of people guys that are come available. So, um you know, where we at? I you know, I don't know. We'll see. Our team hasn't been together. We haven't practiced one time. Um you know, we like the players that we've added in free agency. We like the players that we've added in the draft. We think they're going to mel mesh well with um the the core group that we have here. Um but we got to get on the grass. We have we we got to get on the grass and we got to get a lot of new learning with uh new coaches and and get our team together. Um you know, and I know our guys will be ready to do that. Do you feel like the roster's in a better place than it was last season? I do, yeah. Marty, I'm curious what areas like specifically? Uh because we've added good players in free agency and we added good players in the draft. Uh last year, Calais was one of the most prolific defenders in the in the trenches. So, as you start to get through the next phases of the off season, what have your conversations with him been about maybe playing in season 19 and if so, if this is a place he's considering? Yeah, we've uh you know, we've been in contact with Calais and we're kind of just you know, wait and see mode, you know, we'll see. Um uh he certainly uh earned that right and uh really enjoyed our year last year with him and so, you know, we'll see what that leads to down the road. Is it hard to for you to look at the what on paper what you have and judge it in terms of and then against what you see on the field? Like have have you learned to not do that? Does that Does that make sense? Like right now you're right now you're looking at your roster and you know, like, oh, this is a good team, but you don't really know how good it is until you get on the field. Like Is that something you learned throughout your career not to do? Is that something you did earlier you still do it or what? I mean, I would say, you know, 31 other teams are probably looking at their team right now and saying they've gotten better and and and have an improved. Um and in all reality, none of us know, you know, none of us know until we get out on the field in September. Um and how you know, how we mesh, how we perform, um if we stay healthy, like all those things. So, um you know, I think everybody can say the same, but until you're out there competing and then and when things mean something, you don't really know.
