Um but also he's probably blocked as good of guys in practice like with the defensive line that they had coming out of there last year. Um he's he's saw good competition throughout his whole career. So, um, you know, with the with that with the tackle position, it's it's one that we work all our guys, both sides, and that'll be no different for Jaden. >> Just going off that, you bring back Elijah Wilkinson. Is that someone you see right now as a starting right tackle, just given what you guys did in the draft and other moves? >> Um, yeah, I mean, Elijah, you know, Elijah started 16 games or something last year for Atlanta. So, yeah, I think he'll certainly be in the mix. um you know, not really naming starters anywhere right now, but I think Elijah will definitely have a have a chance there. Um Elijah's another guy who he's played a lot of ball. He's played at different positions. He started, you know, the first go around with us, he was inside at guard. Um he's also played a lot of tackle in his career, so like the versatility that he has, but yeah, he'll definitely be in the mix at right tackle. >> Day always seems to be a little more like volatile in terms of like the the player talent and the dart post and stuff, but you guys have found talent pretty much all three prior drafts on day three. Is there a common denominator you find with all of these like round guys to have them see the success they have in the NFL? >> Um, no. I just think, you know, we have a pretty good process. We put a lot of work into it. Him and I, Rob Kissle, spend a lot of hours up there watching the tape of later round guys. Um, I don't think that's universal through everybody's draft process where um, the top level decision makers pour into the late rounds as much as they do the early rounds. Um, we got a lot of good scouts who who have conviction on some of these guys. We have an analytics department who helps guide us. You know, they got their systems, all their different charts, their Bellstar system, whatever they use. But so we get a lot of input from a lot of people and we take it seriously. You know, um, as a lifetime scout, I hate when people like, ah, it's just a six or seven, who cares? Like, really? I can name you a lot of good players who were found in those rounds who end up mattering for their team. So, I think as long as you emphasize it, you know, you should be able to do it pretty well. >> Sorry. We talked to Monty yesterday about Carson playing in some high pressure games and moments. You have a number of guys who played in the playoff and then even Caleb's game at LSU was high pressure. You know, how do you as a scout kind of evaluate or where do you put playing in big games, big moments on your list of I guess intangibles and whatnot? >> Well, I think it's important, you know, clutch play, you you could label it that, but it's more so, you know, you're looking for matchups, too. Who's the guy playing against? it could be a big game and he's got a weak opponent and he goes off in that game. But, um, you know, it's really the matchups of, you know, Carson Becks going against Texas A&M's defense or, you know, Ohio State's defense, things like that, um, that you're looking at as much as what is the stage, you know what I mean? >> Along those lines, um, I think you guys drafted three or four guys that played in the Shrine Bowl particularly and you had mentioned earlier about Proctor. you get to see them against those guys. Like the ability to see those guys in those all-star games against guys that are going in the draft and maybe are a little bit higher than even if they played in a big conference because those are the best of the best. I mean, how important are those games? And do you guys take a good chunk of what you're getting out when you go to these these all-star games? >> Yeah, I mean, I think any exposure you get is important. The thing about all-star games is you get or your scouts get to go to these games and watch the guys consecutive practices in a row, which you don't really do at schools. You you might hit a school in August, hit it again in October, hit it again maybe late November or something, but they're watching guys practice. Boom, boom, boom. Uh, so they get a feel for like the competition. Some guys will improve over the course of this, you know, hey, this guy's improving. If he can do that, there's more there. And the other thing is like we have our coaches at these games. Chris Cook worked the East West Shrine game. He knows Jaden from that game. So, he can tell us, "Hey, the guy was really good in the meeting room." He learned here, here's this technique that he picked up pretty quickly. I was teaching more, you know, vice versa. If it's negative impact, something like that. Clearly, it wasn't in that case, but uh so that is um very valuable to us. But it's not necessarily any more important than any other one, but you you get a a good experience when you dial in on that stuff. Dave, with Carson Shy, he was talking about how much pride he takes in playing special teams, but in what ways can you see his linebacker instincts when you play special teams, >> run hit, I mean, that's the name of the game. Like, you don't see the guy putting the brakes on before he runs through somebody's face. And that's what special teams is, you know what I mean? So, uh, linebacker obviously is a position where everybody leans on that position for special teams play. And when a guy has that background, like usually know the guy's tough, you usually know he'll work hard, whether he can run or not, like all things that translate to defense eventually. You know, >> you said your undrafted class won't be very big. Why? What goes into that decision? >> Just really roster number. You know, our roster was at a point where um we didn't have a ton of room. So, you know, it's it really comes down to that. I think we'll be six to eight somewhere in there. >> How do you say you approach the draft? You're very big on like best player available, but do you go into a draft thinking, hey, I want to accomplish this. I want to maybe like satisfy this group. And if you did have any of those goals, did you accomplish them? Yeah, I mean I think I think really the the the main goal of of any draft is just to improve the talent level and this is the biggest um roster building time of the year. These three days, you know, that's um you know how many players you're going to be able to add and um there's no better no bigger time that you get to add this volume of players. And so, you know, I think we go in um, you know, having feel for our roster, having a feel for what it looks like, but in the end, all we want to do is add talent, add competition, and just improve the the construction of our roster overall. >> Mont, you've said throughout the offseason that you want to kind of build the foundation for this team, but you also want to build a team that can compete [clears throat] in 2026. Where do you kind of feel like you're at um, you know, now that the primary roster building windows of the offseason are done? >> Uh, yeah. I mean, I' like I I' I'd say the roster building never really ends. You know, it's a it's a constant evolving. Um, you know, we won't get into too much competition this spring. There really is no competition, I should say. Um, that the real competition won't start. But, I mean, there's going to be players that come available next week that um, you know, because of the draft, because of free or undrafted free agent signing, there's going to be another round of PE guys that are come available. So, um, you know, where we're at, I you know, I don't know. We'll see. our team hasn't been together. We haven't practiced one time. Um, you know, we like the players that we've added in free agency. We like the players that we've added in the draft. We think they're going to me mesh well with um the the core group that we have here. Um, but we got to get on the grass. We we we got to get on the grass and we got to get a lot of new learning with uh new coaches and and get our team together. Um, you know, and I know our guys will be ready to do that. >> You feel like the roster is in a better place than it was last season? >> I do. Yeah. I'm curious what area was like specifically >> uh because we've added good players in free agency and we added good players in the draft. >> Uh last year Kas was one of the most prolific defenders in the in the trenches and so as you start to get through the next phases of the offseason. What have your conversations with him been about maybe playing in season 19 and if so if this is a place he's considering? >> Yeah, we've uh you know we've been in contact with Quas and we're kind of just in a wait and see mode. You know, we'll see. um uh he certainly uh earned that right and uh really enjoyed our year last year with him and so you know we'll see what that leads to down the road. >> Is it hard to for you to look at what on paper what you have >> and judge it in terms of and then against what you see on the field like have you learned to not do that? Does that that make sense? Like right now right now you're looking at your roster and you're like oh this is a good team but you don't really know how good it is until you get on the field. Is that something you learned throughout your career not to do? Is that something you did early to still do it or what? >> I mean, I would say, you know, 31 other teams are probably looking at their team right now and saying they've gotten better and and have improved. Um, and in all reality, none of us know, you know, none of us know until we get out on the field in September. Um, and how, you know, how we mesh, how we perform, um, if we stay healthy, like all those things. So, um, you know, I think everybody can say the same, but until you're out there competing and and when things mean something, you don't really know. >> Gentlemen, thank you. >> Awesome. Thank you guys.

title: Ryan Poles, Ben Johnson recap 2026 NFL Draft | Press Conference
text: All right, I'll start off by just uh want to thank our staff. I think one of the cool parts of a draft process is everyone's got a part. Everyone leans into the process. Um and and and puts in the work and on draft day you see it all come together and um our staff is amazing at what they do, the time that they spend on it and the ability to work together. Um, we found great alignment and that created a lot of good clarity which resulted in in a good draft and I know we got better uh as a football team. We added competition and usually when you add competition uh good things happen. So I don't know if you have anything to say but >> yeah, you know, I just piggyback on it. I I couldn't be uh more pleased with with Ryan and his crew. Uh these scouts, they went they went out this fall and they collected all kinds of information and uh I mean I think they absolutely nailed it. We found guys that fit our DNA and what we want to be about. Um we found it round one through round six there, our last pick and and even in some of these guys we're picking up right now. U I think we're still finding our type of guys. So that was important for us. you would you would hope from year one to year two with this this coaching staff and the personnel department we're so much further along than we were a year ago at this time. So that's that's what's encouraging to me and and Ryan and uh really look forward to to seeing these guys hit the grass here in a couple weeks. >> Significant roster change since January. Where do you see improvement? Where do you sense the football team's gotten better since last season? Well, I I'm going to start with uh continuity with the coaching staff because I I really do think um the ability for us, a a group of guys, a lot of which we hadn't coached together before. Um looking to to unify that vision and bring it to life the way that we did last fall, we're going to be so much better off having gone through the cutups. Um, I know we've really refined and made it a a big effort here this springtime already to to get the fundamentals, the techniques to another level in terms of how we're teaching it and how we're coaching it. And so, I think it really starts there, at least from my lens. Um, I think we'll be better teachers of of not only the scheme, but also, um, just the vision of what we want our brand of football to look like. And so, uh, in terms of the personnel side, the the roster, um, I think we have, just like Ryan said, created competition really across the board. Um, and I I really expect some of these young players that we already had in the program to take a huge jump from year one to year two of this coaching staff. Uh, and then we create a lot of competition really at every position group. So, >> talk about the DNA of this class. What is the common thread to you that you see in these players you've got the last three? Yeah. Well, I think Jeff King hit it a couple days ago and that's that's really we're looking for highlevel competitors. Guys that if you took football away from, they really don't know what to do with themselves. It's it's a huge part. They eat it, they sleep it, they breathe it. And uh I think we're able to identify those type of guys. And when you have guys like that, they usually find a way to come out on top. >> How similar How similar is that? >> What strength you set >> at safety? Um, well, that's what you kind of from from being an offensive guy, it's rare that you see a safety as a guy that you really worry about. And yet, it was pretty quickly that you could turn on his tape and and realize he's always around the football. He's got a knack for the football. Um, he's a great tackler and when he does it, he does it with violence. And so, to me, it his style of play showed up. I thought Oregon did a great job putting him in a position to succeed and uh and he really thrived in that system and it goes back to his Purdue days as well. I mean he just for three straight years high level production and then when you combine that with the athlete that he is, the the football IQ uh to us it was a no-brainer um when he was there. But I really do think he's going to be a guy that one of those few those rare safety types that that uh coordinators are going to have to account for. Ben, given how much is on a center's plate in the NFL, but particularly in your offense, what's the benefit here for Logan getting to come in maybe learn for a while under Garrett and maybe take his time before he becomes a starter? >> Yeah, well, I I think uh we were really smitten with Logan throughout the process. You know, Dan Roshark, Kyle Dean, um they went out and and went to several places this springtime to make sure we we could identify the guys that we felt really good about and and obviously Logan was at the the top of the list for us. And so we felt convicted as a staff um coaching staff and and personnel side that he was our guy. Uh the the mental is topnotch. Um we saw all the traits that we're looking for uh whether it's the run game or a pass pro and we brought him in for a top 30 and I think that's when it really solidified it for us that yeah he he's got the makeup. Um the guys at Iowa were raving about him and then just the next level in terms of uh football IQ as well. So, I I think uh none of us have any qualms that he'll be able to download the information and uh once again, it's just another spot that we'll have high level competition at. >> Coach, you d you draft a potential future center. You draft a tight end who has a specific role in your system. You draft a kick returner and maybe a third, fourth, fifth type of receiver, guys type of player. Is that indicative of you knowing exactly the types of pieces that you can use for certain particular roles in your offense? And then Ryan, if I can ask this of you as well, is that a different place to be in in terms of roster building to be at a space where you can use draft capital on specific types of pieces for specific roles on the team? >> Well, yeah. Yeah, there's certainly things going into the off season. Um, you know, once again, Ryan did a great job through free agency making sure that we patched any major holes so that we could go into this draft and feel like we we could take the guys however the board laid out. And uh you know the one thing I I do feel pretty confident about is this is what you know you feel good about just tight end position for example you got Coloulston Lovelin who you love. You got Cole KT who you love. Well we're really targeted at that third tight end spot. What does it look like? What do we value the most? Um and so what is most appealing to us might not be most appealing to the next guy. Same thing with the wide receiver discussion that you're talking about. what's most appealing for us. And as we fill out that room, knowing that Rome and Luther are big components of it, we want to find guys that help complement the skill sets and uh and like I said, the non-negotiable is is be the type of players that we want to be and and so that we can bring the vision of the the football to life. >> Ryan, I'm sorry. Can I get a response from Ryan on the second part of that question? I I think the biggest thing is just our communication and the communication with the front office and and the coaching staff as we're watching these players and and and handing that off to our coaches. We're we're talking about how how are we going to use this player in our system? How how would you use them? Where can we um emphasize their strengths of their game? Um so we talk about that a lot and and that goes into the draft so we have clarity in terms of how that player is going to come in and and impact our team. Ben, how is how is it for you to be in this position as the offensive play caller and have so much direct input into the players being picked compared to before uh when you were with Detroit, but now you have such a big voice in the room that you're getting to really handpick guys that you need for things you want to do. >> Well, yeah, I think that's any head coach in the NFL. You know, they have a good partnership um with the with the general manager and and what we're looking to do is have a unified vision on on how we want to build this football team. And so, just like Brian alluded to, we've got constant communication of what we want this thing to look like. And um I do think we're a lot further along, you know, just in terms of our vision and uh year two here than it was a year ago. So, that's what that's what fires me up the most. Ben, >> what did you learn about in your first year as head coach? What did you learn that helped you focus the DNA or, you know, at least being clear super clear about the DNA of the kind of player you want? Uh Ryan mentioned the other day that it's it's just kind of a little more focused than it had been. >> Well, well, yeah, I think it starts with we know what's currently in our roster on in our locker room more than what we did a year ago. We're still getting to know the players. Um, and so I I think once you've figured that piece out, you know, you have your conversations with coach High Tower and coach Coach Allen and um, you know, how they see it as well and how we want to shape it and how we can make it better, how we can make the whole environment um, just a little bit little bit better. And so I think that's really what what goes into it. Um, we we know our our guys and so we know what we want to mix in there a little bit more often >> with with today's picks. give us like a little rundown about how it all came together and you traded up twice and what you like about the three defensive guys you got today. >> Yeah, we were just monitoring you know the back end of this draft and you know there was names that we were real convicted about that again we had clarity on what their role was going to be um in terms of their opportunity when they when they get here. U so we were a little bit more aggressive with with those names. Um, so with, you know, Malik, um, he's he's someone that we talked about, Al, DA, and I, um, we like the way that he covers. We like the play style. Um, and we think there's there's room for him to continue to improve, too. So, add competition to that quarter room. Um, and we think that he can positively impact us and give us more depth early and as he grows into something bigger. We'll see how that goes. Uh, and then Keshan, you know, a player that physical brand of football, um, has really good size, can run. And then again, his ability both play to to play the linebacker position and also help on special teams. You know, High Tower has a huge say in in this whole deal, too. We want to make sure those guys can perform on special teams, which is going to help them make the active roster, which is important. Um, and then finishing up with with Jordan. Um, again, the real cool part of this whole process, you go through uh, you know, your your uh, winter uh, film work and then you get back from the combine and then you got some guys that maybe non-combine guys that that do really good at proday that pop up on your radar. Um, Jordan was one of them and as we got his name around the building and we were working together with the coaches, there's a level of excitement. Um, so he was a player that we identified that we wanted to go get. We didn't want to wait any longer. I don't think he would have lasted to us in the seventh. So, we're a little bit more aggressive. Went and got him. Um, and you could tell with the energy that came through the building and especially our Dline coaches, they were they were fired up. So, um, really excited how we finish this draft. >> Savian, what about his game stimulates your creativity offensively? What what's a realistic way that that you can involve him early? Well, yeah, he he's got a unique skill set just in terms of he's a 4-2 guy and those guys don't grow on trees and um and so it's easy to look at because that flashes up and everyone sees it, but yet when you turn on the tape, uh it's more than just being able to run deep routes. the the versatility that he showed uh both at Mississippi State and at LSU from the back field um whether it's running routes or getting handoffs and then the the returning um aspect of it. I I think it all adds up and uh you know, coach Randle, myself, Press Taylor, we all have a vision of how this guy could could really help us. And as I talked about, it's it's a complement to what Rome does best, Luther does best, Khif does best, and so um he's a guy that we really feel like can play a key component in what we want to do this year. >> Ryan and Francis St. Paul described mannerisms you have when you're watching T. >> Yeah. What are they? Well, Francis said you do some rocking and Are you aware of the things that that you do when you >> Well, I mean, we're sitting in the chairs for a long time, so I just got to shift position. But, um, >> no, I it's it's weird. I feel like, you know, I'll sit next to Ryan when those scouts are in there. And, uh, I I almost feel like we can feel each other a little bit, which is unique for for a couple guys that really haven't done it together for for a very long time yet. And so, um, there's just I think we we he and I view players very similarly. and and so uh I'm sure we we do kind of feed off each other a little bit. >> You you and Ryan both were pretty open all offseason about needing pass rush improvement. The fact that you didn't sign a big name one free agency, didn't draft an edge rusher, how is it going to get better with the same guys who were out there last year? >> Well, we we're certainly going to coach better than what we did a year ago. And I like I said before, it starts there. We've made a concerted effort in how we're going to get that done. Um I'm uh we were excited about the guys that uh ended up finishing the season on IR. The trajectory that they were on both Dio and Shamar when you look at it from the start of the season to the point where they both got injured. We saw growth and we saw them trend in the right direction in terms of uh what we want to see on game day. I think uh I think Sweat had one of his better years in the NFL. whether that shows up in the sack total or not, he's he's a very complete player uh both run game and pass game and and I think you saw tremendous growth from Booker when we were finally able to get him back as well. So, um the combination of us being able to coach better and and those guys taking the next step as part of this system, um you know, I I I think we got some pretty good pieces to work with >> that on that front strategy at uh quarterback as far as bringing in young quarterbacks behind Caleb and Tyson. And did you get some scouting intel from Caleb on uh Miller Moss? >> Oh, that's out already. Uh yeah, no, we did really good work. Uh again, JT and and some of our scouts got together and um watched, you know, a large stack of quarterbacks and trying to identify ones that could come here and and compete and perform. Um it's important to to keep working that that quarterback room and and making sure that we got guys that can come here and and again add to the competition and guys that we want to pour into so that they can develop um and then we'll see where it goes. Ryan, Ryan, with the um need for a defensive line, was it uh difficult to stay disciplined to the board? And will you go back and re-evaluate whether you would have liked to be more aggressive in parts or just what's your uh take about the defensive line in general and your approach to it? >> Yeah. Uh I thought we were we were disciplined. Again, we said this a few times, just following the board and the best player that was available to us. Um, I think one thing that we take real seriously is is each year we'll go back and and review our process and review the draft and and see where we could have done something a little bit different. Um, learn from that and then just keep getting better as we go. But I like the approach that we had. Um, came away with some really good players. Um, and like I've said before with with any position, we're going to stay active, see what opportunities pop up, and if we can improve our football team, we'll do it. Ben, throughout the process, as you're talking about the players that you identify having that competitiveness, what are things you do, whether you're talking to the player or you're talking to Ryan, your scouts, how do you kind of figure out guys that that tick the way that you're looking for this locker room? >> Well, I always think it starts with the tape. And so, it doesn't take long. I think normally within the first 20 plays, you you kind of see whether those traits show up. And if they don't, then you keep looking. You keep looking. Um, but eventually you kind of make a decision whether whether you should stop or not. And so I think our guys have done a great job identifying who those guys are. Um, you know, we look at the personal character, the football character, the makeup and all that and and that checks the boxes. And then, you know, fortunately, we're able to get some guys in for top 30s, get to know them a little bit better. The combine's a huge part of that process as well. And like I alluded to before, we we sometimes we send coaches out to to meet with guys individually as well uh at individual pro days. So, I I think we do a pretty good job, but it it always starts with the tape in my opinion. I think that's uh that's always the the number one thing that we should be looking for. >> And with Rous's tape specifically, what was that? What were those things that popped to you? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, he's he is a finisher through the whistle. And uh I think that showed up on a consistent basis. It didn't matter who he was blocking. Could be a big guy, could be a little DB, and uh he consistently finished through the whistle each and every play. Um, and you always love it when you when you take a player and you get a text message from somebody. One of his coaches at Stanford said he he will he will crush himself to do whatever he can to help the football team and it just verifies what you all already thought about the thought about the players. So, feel good about that one. >> Um, you said with a defensive line you expect better results because it'll be coached better this year. What what needs to change with the coaching, the approach? like what when you got met up with the coaches this offseason. What did you determine would go in a different direction? How do you get there? >> Well, it's the the deal when you're a first year staff, not everything's going to look the way you want it to look. And uh it didn't matter if it was offense or defense. You know, fortunately, Coach High Totower had been here, so he had had a lot of uh time on task with a number of guys in his unit. Uh but for us on offense and defense, you look at the self scout and it doesn't look the way we want it to look. And so to me, that's a reflection of coaching. Um and so we're going to we we made a concerted effort on both sides of the ball there to make sure that we're going to get it to look more the way that we want it to look. And so um that's natural. I mean, I don't think year one when I was a first year play caller, uh did it look the way it looked year two or year three. So um that's natural. That's that's how you get better. We're always striving to improve and and uh and I think the things that we emphasize we're going to see improvement at. >> Dan and Pat to close us out. >> And back to Courtney's earlier question on Logan, whether it's in his rookie season or 2027, what's his path to becoming a starter that can be reliable, the role with all that you put on that position? >> Yeah, we we'll we'll see. Um we do load guys up and and that was something that we talked about uh when he was here on the top 30. He knows that that that center position is I don't want to say it's unique to to what we ask them to do, but um I would say we're probably on the higher end in terms of NFL teams and and what we ask those guys to to be able to handle. And so um I know he's up for the challenge. We'll we'll uh we'll see where he's at when he gets here and how quickly he takes to it. But um yeah, you certainly you take a player where you take him and and you see a you see a future for him. There's no no question about it. I don't know that we've mentioned Caleb Williams name yet, but she might be a record about Miller Mos. >> Oh, about Miller Moss. Okay, we brought Bill. Um, how do all these pieces fit around Caleb, whether it's a center he can grow with, a tight end that can help protect him and catch passes for him? How do those pieces fit together with a quarterback who you know a lot more about today than you did a year ago today? >> Yeah, well, I think uh just for his sake, it's going to give us a lot of flexibility here on offense. um you know, we're going to have the ability to go heavy, go 13 personnel, keep keep a defense in in their base uh structure or we we're going to be able to get a little bit lighter and we got speed on the outside. So, I think it gives us gives him a lot of versatility to work with and we can dictate some terms to to the defense and and uh make sure that we're always attacking. Um, his big goal here is going to be to make sure he can get up to speed with these new pass catchers and continue to refine his chemistry with the guys that we've already had, which he's been he's been working at already all uh this offseason, last few weeks. He and I kind of talked about I think he got all the guys out in California and um so I know he's been working working on that, but um we'll hit the grass. We got one more week of phase one. we'll hit the hit the grass for phase two and and we'll really be able to hone in on some of those details of of where he can get better with his teammates. >> Awesome. Thank you.

title: Jordan van den Berg on his journey from South Africa to Chicago | Press Conference
text: Hey Jordan, congratulations. Welcome to Chicago. Um, it seems like you've got a pretty unique athletic background with family members who are big-time athletes. Uh, we were just talking to one of the area scouts and he was saying that your grandmother was a swimmer, your grandfather was a was a weight lifter, bodybuilder. Is that correct? >> Yes. So, I'm fortunate to come from a really athletic background. My grandfather was a five-time Mr. South Africa um bodybuilder, best bodybuilder in South Africa. title: Dan Morgan and Dave Canales post-draft press conference | Carolina Panthers
text: Good to see every every everybody. Um brain's a little fried right now. Um First off, just kind of want to thank the staff, uh the scouting staff, the coaches, football operations, everybody involved for what we feel is a successful draft. Uh we felt like we definitely got better. We challenged the roster in a lot of spots. Um gained gained a lot of depth in a lot in a lot of areas. Um so yeah, we feel feel good about what we accomplished during the draft and excited about things moving forward and we're obviously headed in the right direction, so um with that, I'll open it up to any questions. We'll kick things off with Joe Person. Hey Dan. Uh um What's up, Joe? Good good to see you, man. You too. Get getting a little dark over here. All right, you're good. Um once you traded back to 227, um what about the the I heard you talk about um challenging the roster and building depth. Did did you draft anyone this weekend you think will start from day one? Um you know, I think everybody that we drafted, you know, I think they'll all have the opportunity to compete um and that's what we're all about here, myself and coach and the rest of the staff. We want to bring guys in to challenge the roster and have them compete and you know, we brought we brought in a bunch of competitors during this draft and they're going to have a chance to compete and show us what they can do and uh it'll be fun to watch. Which of these guys do you think has the best chance to make the biggest, earliest impact? Uh I think it's up to them. You know, I think I'm uh excited about all the guys that we drafted, otherwise, you know, we wouldn't have drafted them, so they're all going to have the opportunity to come in and compete and we're excited to see what they can do. Are you considering bringing in another uh undrafted quarterback? Uh potentially. Potentially, we'll we'll do that and have four quarterbacks, which we really haven't had since I don't think we've been here, but yeah, there's definitely the potential for for that. You think it's likely? Yeah, I do. Okay. Yeah. Alex Zietlow. Hey Dan, congrats on um getting through another NFL draft. Thanks. What's up, Alex? What's up, man? Um uh particularly on day three, there seemed to be a couple guys who um uh who fell to you guys. Um particularly uh Zaquandre Whiteley and um and Sam Hecht. Are those two guys, when you had the opportunity to draft them, were were you surprised that they were still available at um when you got the chance to take them? Uh yeah, a little bit. You know, I think uh I think you saw us kind of maneuver around the board a little bit. Uh just looking at our board, you know, we had a handful players that we had up there, so we're like, "Hey, we like these guys." Like they're all guys that we feel like can help us, so we're like, "Let's trade back. Let's gain more picks, gain more value." And you know, we did that and then and it worked out in our favor at the end. Specifically about Zaquandre, how do you see him fitting into the this defense? Yeah, you know, just a big, long, physical guy. Um he fits the DNA that we want, the type of competitor that we want. Um he can play the post, he can play up in the box, he can do a lot of things for our defense that we're excited about. Any more questions? Cassie. Hey Dan, how's it going? What's up, Cassie? Um you had a couple of guys today that made it through college or at least the last couple of years without a single penalty. Is that just kind of a coincidence or is that something that y'all value and look at? I mean, obviously, we don't want penalties. Um I think it's more a coincidence than than anything. Um but honestly, I didn't even really know that. That's kind of cool, though. Yeah, I think it was uh Whiteley and Hecht made it through without a penalty in college or at least last couple of years. And then on Will Lee specifically, he he comes off the tape like really just kind of tenacious. How important is that in a safety back there? Yeah, you know, corner, safety, um that's what we want, you know, that's our identity. You know, we want to be physical, we want to be tough, we want to be competitive and you know, we we're drafting those type of guys in our culture and um you know, I think every one of those guys that we drafted, you know, from the first round all the way down to the seventh, they they embody that. Daron Gantt followed by Mike Kaye. Dan, specifically to Hecht at center, what did you guys see in him that you like and and how do you see him competing right out of the gate? Yeah, he's going to have a chance to compete. Um I think first and foremost, you see his initial quickness. Uh he's really good with angles. You know, he can reach guys. He's good with his hands, getting his hands inside, controlling blockers and staying staying sticky on blocks. Um I would say is the biggest thing with him, staying on his feet, keeping his balance. Um he's another guy that can work to the second level. He can get out in space as a puller. Um so there's a lot of things that we like about him. Was it a priority for you this weekend to to make that room not only deeper, but younger as you look at the makeup of the offensive line as a whole? Yeah, you know, I I definitely think we need to add some youth in there, you know, on the interior and outside at tackle and feel like we accomplished that and you know, we'll do some things in undrafted free agency as well that'll again add to the competition and the and the depth out there. Hey Dan, thanks for doing this. Yeah. I'm setting myself up to be made fun of because of how I pronounce the kids' name uh by Joe. Uh Jackson, the guy you just added from Miami of Ohio. Um do you see him as kind of a special teams cog or what what's your outlook on him? He doesn't have a lot of playing time prior to last year. Yeah, good player, uh really good instincts. He can run, he plays fast. Uh he sees it really well. Uh a guy that we're obviously excited about. You know, I think he's definitely going to be able to contribute on special teams and again, like like every area, like he's going to have a chance to compete and show us what he can do. And then with Will Lee, um do you see him primarily working outside boundary wise? I know he brought up how much he likes doing press man, but obviously that's not something you guys do a ton. Um do you guys see him as like a long-term outside cornerback? Yeah, um you know, I think obviously, I'll leave that up to the coaches for what they want to do with him. Um at Texas A&M, he played on the outside and he's really good at press and and I think he's a guy that as he continues to grow and mature in the game, he'll be able to, you know, figure out off coverage and some of the things that we do schematically. I think he's just a really good fit for us by the way he plays, the temperament he plays with, the swag he plays with out there. Uh just a guy that we really loved. Joe Person followed by Sheena Quick. Um Dan is Dan or Dave can address this or both of you. Kind of following up on Daron's question. Were was this a draft where you you guys wanted to, you know, kind of look long-term more so maybe than than short-term? Uh I'll answer that. I mean, I won't For for me, it's always about right now. Uh this season and what we're doing and um trying to make sure that we can get the most out of our guys that we currently have. We always start with our roster, but then, you know, trying to find guys that fit the traits and characteristics, personality of who the Panthers are. Um and that's what we were looking for is just get more of that and uh it's going to be the same thing every year. You know, can we how can we make the 2026 Panthers the best possible unit that we can make it and um if we have guys that, you know, bring a certain skill set at any position uh to give them a chance to compete and be out there, you know, we just felt feel like it elevates the whole group. And then back to Dan. Um is there's a lot all every year, I really since you took over, people uh and you have drafted tight ends, but I there's this feeling I think that you guys need to go get a tight end a number one tight end. Is that shared in in the building or I don't know. You you addressed it a little bit last week. >> Yeah, we have a we have a lot of confidence in the guys that are on our roster and I said that before, you know, with Tommy and with Mitch and with Jatavion and James Mitchell and you know, we we have some guys that we're excited about and you know, again, we'll always look for, you know, avenues to make the roster better. If we feel like we need to, you know, figure figure out tight end and bring a different skill set in, then we'll do that, but right now, we feel good about it. And then Dan, any positions where you feel like you're still maybe a little light, whether it's inside linebacker, even corner? Uh you know, I think again, we're we're always going to find ways. We're never going to be content. We're never we're never just going to sit there. We're just going to try to add as much depth and competition to the roster as possible and you know, we'll we'll keep doing that moving forward. Good afternoon, guys. How are you? Good. How you doing? Um just a question about uh Lee and Whiteley. What specifically did you guys see in those two players that made them a fit for the corner and safety rooms that you guys have right now? Lee Lee and Wheatley? Yeah, Will Lee. Oh, yeah. Um, you want to go? >> Yeah, I'll take it. Yeah. Um, you know, we look for play style first and foremost. Um, trying to project, you know, the the athletic ability to contribute is obviously a big part of it. But then, once we kind of know and identify guys that we feel like can can impact us and can play in the NFL from an athletic standpoint, then we go to play style. And you know, Will Lee, Dan kind of talked about it a little bit, the length, the aggressiveness, his ability to play physical at the at the attack point, whether it's on bubble screens or getting involved in the run game. We ask our corners to tackle, you know, and and be a part of the fits in our system with our cracker place rules and different things like that. So, we felt like he really fit that mold. And then, for Z Wheatley, he's just a really instinctive player, physical player, shows up downhill, takes really good angles, runs downhill. He's all over the field and you know, just that kind of activity on the back half is it's really crucial for how we play football and and guys being able to see the formation, anticipate concepts, and then show up physically and play with that type of attitude that we're looking for. We had a great time you know, meeting with Zakhia at the combine and just kind of picking his brain about what he knew, what he was looking for and where he came from and how he's become the player that he's come. And we just loved all the background and everything and it really shows on on film and he was one of my favorite guys just through the process to see him in the play style that he brought. Thanks, guys. We have time for just a few more. We'll go back to Mike Kaye. Hey Dave, this running back class is not particularly deep at least from the outside looking in and in the selections that were made. You've had Jonathan in the program for about a week. And and and Montrell's another guy who, you know, played at a really high level in college and and is is finding his way in the pros. But we were able to bring those guys in. We're excited to see what they can do. And when we start with this process, we always, you know, as we're looking at players in the draft, we kind of look at them compared to our roster, compared to the guys we have. Who is this guy competing with in this room? Like where do we see them being able to try to affect it? And we got a bunch of guys that we're really excited about. And you know, of course you talked about Jonathan and and Trevor, you know, um, in in that conversation as well. And and we have high hopes for Jonathan, you know, and and he looks great right now. Can't wait to, you know, in the smartest way possible get him out there and expose him at the right time and and get him accustomed to the things that we're doing. But um, yeah, love that group. I love what Bernie Parmalee's doing with them and and how they attack it. And you know, we kind of tell them you set the tone for the offense. And so, we love the way those guys are built. And we haven't been able to talk to you about it yet, but Trevon and JT do you think both participating in the program as well? Yeah. Um, the Trevon came back he's he's doing really great in terms of getting back out there. JT's been cleared. He's doing more and more. So, but right now as we know, you know, they're it's weight room and and meetings right now. So, until we get onto the field and kind of move them around, we still got to be smart about all that stuff. Yeah. Thank you. All right, guys. That's all the questions we have for you today. Thank you so much for taking the time. Thanks, guys. All right, thank you. >> [music] [music]

title: Matt LaFleur 1-on-1: 'It's an exciting time for the Packers' | 2026 NFL Draft
text: Hey everybody, we are joined by Packers head coach Matt LaFleur. Matt, welcome and thanks for being here. Do you feel you got you got better over the past couple days? Yeah, absolutely. I think anytime you can add talent to your roster, it's an exciting time for the Packers. Now, you guys drafted six players and four of them were defensive [music] players. The first three defensive players, is Jonathan Gannon, your new defensive coordinator, a happy camper? >> Oh, yeah. He's always happy, but he's even happier now. So, I kind of had the feeling that that's the route we were going to go going into the draft and certainly we had a lot of high value marks on those specific players and we feel like we did a great job with that. Now, this past off season, a number of changes on the coaching staff. How was that group coming together and becoming the team within a team that you have needed to be? Yeah, I think it's been great. I mean, we've spent a lot of time in the meeting room together and now it's our ability to go out there and and teach whatever we're going to teach to our players. Matt, those first three defensive players that you drafted, Colby Wooden, [music] Carrington Valentine, potential contributors as rookies. How do you look at that? Well, I think every guy that comes in here has to earn their opportunity, has to earn their their reps. So, but we feel good about those guys coming in and competing right away. With the addition of Trey Smack, the last of your draft picks, the kicker from Florida, is that a real deal competition at that position? Yeah, absolutely. Just like every other position, you're always trying to to bring in guys to compete and and make your roster better and certainly we had him as the highest rated kicker in the draft and we're lucky that he was still available [music] when we got him. Somewhere over the last couple of days, you were able to find the time to resign Jayden Reed. That is big stuff. I mean, that young man is just a winner, isn't he? He certainly is and I think you see his contributions to our not only in our offense, but our football team when he's available. Certainly missed a lot of time last last season with that collarbone and when he's not in the lineup, we feel that. As things stand now, you're looking at a revamped offensive line. Sean Ryan at center, Anthony Belton at right guard and then Jordan Morgan at left tackle. Are you pretty comfortable with that group? Yeah, I think so. I think it's going to be an important off season for those guys, just like every off off season is, but you know, just to have five guys that you know where [music] they're going to be cuz certainly last year at this time we had a left tackle competition and [music] then we went with what we thought was our five best to go out there and compete across the board and but Jordan a year ago showed us that he is more than capable of holding that position. Matt, can you give us any kind of an update on your injured guys, in particular, Micah Parsons, Tucker Kraft, those types of individuals? Yeah, we've been in in constant contact with those guys and our medical staff and I would say that they're coming along nicely, but there's still a long road ahead of them. Are you concerned at all about the backup quarterback position? We've been spoiled, no question with Malik, but are you concerned at all right now at this point? I wouldn't say concerned. I think we're just trying to push these guys to be their best and hopefully, you know, of the two guys that we have, one of these guys can take that step and and really take a hold of that position. Matt, you guys are involved in phase one of the off season program right now. How is that going and what is that all about? Yeah, well, first of all, the participation has been outstanding. We've had the majority of our guys here and they're just I love how they're competing, coming in with a great attitude and I think that's when that is >> [music] >> so important in terms of getting your max results is you got to attack it the right way and with the right mentality and our guys are doing that. I don't know about you, but I find it a real exciting time in the year, but I'm different. Rookie camp coming up. You're looking forward to it. I mean, you kind of get the whole group together and it's kind of cool. Yeah, that it's it'll be our first exposure to these guys and really the way we approach the rookie mini camp is it's more of an onboarding process for our guys, get them in, get them acclimated to the building, get them acclimated to their coaches, support staff, the playbook, obviously each other's an important component to that and then we put them through a couple of different workouts because it's important because a week from that rookie mini camp, they're in with the vets in the phase two. So, that gives them a chance to take what they learn, go on their own for a week, try to improve because a lot of these guys have been training for the combine, so they might not be in the best football shape, but it gives them an opportunity to kind of get a a jump start on what's expected in phase two. Matt, thank you. Appreciate it. Absolutely. Thanks, Larry.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: "Every player in our roster is going to be competing"
text: think of the acquisition of of Taylor Mcgra and what can he do for you guys? What does he add to your quarterback record? >> I just think uh at that point in the draft and again I think Andrew can speak to this more than I can but you're looking for players that have traits, elite traits, which he has something you think you can work with and give yourself a chance to develop. um you hear some great things from not only when he was at Boise or Arkansas terms of how he's wired and uh so we're just looking forward to get to work with him. I know you said that I know you previously said that like uh holding like a a four-way quarterback competition isn't ideal and andrew kind of uh indicated that he needs some polish for this game, but um do you feel comfortable with like the plan going forward to to not only hold this quarterback competition, but to get all the quarterbacks the reps that they need uh the young ones to develop? >> Well, let's just talk about what competition means at every position. every player that's going to be a part of our roster is going to be competing, right? I mean, whoever we bring in, uh, starting with rookie mini camp and then OTAAS's mandatory mini camp and then training camp, but as we've spoken before at any position, that doesn't mean equal reps. >> I mean, there there has to be some form of a a depth chart, per se. Uh, everybody has a chance to compete. Uh, they just they're not always going to get equal reps, if that makes sense. You know, it's what is a competition? Every guy that's in training camp, every guy that's part of a roster, the amount of reps they get, uh, that's to be determined. >> How how playing the last couple of years for Taylor playing the last couple years under Bob in Bobby's system, how has that sort of gotten him prepared for this level in terms of what what he does schematically, what he asks his quarterbacks to do within that system? Well, first off, coach did a great job of adapting. Um, which really good coordinators do. They adapted. You know, if you look at quarterbacks that coach Petrino's had in the past compared to to this young man, different um they did a great job of adapting to his strengths and you can see that. But I I'm sure there were still still core principles of the expectations that he has for their quarterbacks. And you could see the development over the few the few years, you know, from when he was at Boise. Really developed as a passer. You can you can see that. Always has been able to run and and you can see that in his statistics. You can see when he was at Boise how few of times they threw it compared to where they were at Arkansas, how they felt more comfortable uh with his ability to throw the football down the field. >> Todd, with with Talon, uh Andrew made it clear that you guys view him as a quarterback first, but as as your offensive mind that you are, do you sort of envision or what are some of the other ways that you feel like maybe you can get him involved and get the ball in his hands given the skill set that you highlighted? Well, that remains to be determined. I will say say this that it is very difficult to be elite at one position in the NFL, let alone two. I think uh teams are starting to find that out. >> With obviously your long time reputation as a as a really good quarterback, tutor, guru, uh how much how eager are you to get your hands on a on a quarterback like this with such raw physical ability and just almost kind of like mold him into like whatever he can kind of be. >> Well, I mean it's uh we're excited about any player that we get. Uh so so be to be able to get I I wouldn't just single out him per se other than we're excited with his skill set and coach but Jakeian's excited uh to add someone with his traits that we're hopeful to be able to get, you know, on the field and then see what we got. >> Look at um your offense now, the players you have now compared to when the draft started. title: Anthony Smith Reacts to Being Drafted by the Cowboys | Player Interviews
text: All right, we do have Anthony Smith on the line. Anthony, congratulations on this moment. I know it's a proud day for you and your family. Take us through what's going through your head right now as you are now a member of the Dallas Cowboys. Yes, sir. Man, well, shoot. The first thing I just want to give it to God, man. Like, without him I wouldn't be in this position, man. All the struggles, all the all the trials and tribulations I done went through in college and my family and stuff. And shoot, he brought me on the other side. So, for me and my family, man, this is this is an ecstatic moment, bro. I can't lie. So, I'm feeling good, man. My family's feeling good. I'm just ready to get down to Dallas and play some ball, man. Anthony, you and I have actually talked a couple times during my time covering the American Conference and I've been a big fan of your game for quite some time. For those at the NFL level or the Dallas Cowboys level that may not know, tell them what they're getting in Anthony Smith as a wide receiver at the next level. Shoot, I know they're getting somebody who can take the top off the defense, somebody who's fast, and somebody who loves to compete, ready to work every day. So, shoot, just as a receiver, man, I'm ready to just go get it. Anthony, congratulations. Walk me through the emotions of the weekend. Did you expect to be picked coming in? And then when you finally got the phone call, just talk me through the relief in the moment. Yeah, man. So, shoot. I mean, I did have that faith, man, that I was going to get picked this weekend. Just just having that hope. Um, and then as the weekend went on went on and stuff like that, I just seen the rounds go on and on and stuff like that. And um, I still kept that hope. My family still kept that hope that I was going to get drafted. Um, and then me and my agent had talked and stuff like that. And um, we were kind of prepared to go the UDFA route. And then um, the Cowboys had called me, man. And I walked downstairs to my family and and told them who I was on the phone with and stuff. And I got a lot of family who's Dallas fans. So, when they heard that I was on the phone you guys, ready to get drafted, they were they were so excited, man. So, for me and my family, bro, it's just like it's a crazy process. It's a long process, but it was it was all worth it, bro, for sure. And then you'll be reuniting with Savion Red Jr. Have you talked to Savion yet? Has he shot you a text? He hasn't He hasn't just yet. But me and him talked the other day though, man. Me and him talked the other day just about like him being at the next level, things to expect and stuff like that, and the work that you got to put in and I mean, he's been there for a year. So, he's been pouring into me knowing that this is my goal that I want to get to the NFL and I want to play in the NFL. So, like him just pouring into me and just letting me know the things that I need to get right and and check off the box um, so that I can make those things happen. So, that's my good man for sure. As you reflect back at at at your college journey and and going from NC State to Eastern Carolina, it seems like it kind of you had to go through maybe some struggles there at NC State and then finally blossom there at East Carolina. What really stood out to you about that and and kind of helped you to become the receiver you are now? Yeah, I mean, for me, bro, it's really just maturity and intentionality, man. Just just getting older, you know what I'm saying, learning how to how to really play ball and how to really, you know what I'm saying, the the ins and outs of the offense and stuff like that. And then the intentionality of every day coming in the coming in the building, whether it's treatment, lift, conditioning, practice, that I'm just trying to attack it. Shoot, want to get 1% better each day, man. Just attack it head on. And just compete at everything I do, man. So, You also seem to have an outstanding hair game, Anthony. >> [laughter] >> What what goes into that? Shoot, not much, honestly. I mean, shoot. I I I cut my hair not too long ago. I used to have it super super long, but I I cut it short now. So, a little bit more manageable, easy to maintain. So, It's just natural talent. That's all it is. Yeah, man. Just natural, bro. Just natural. >> Hey, Anthony, congratulations. Not sure how I can transition to a much better question there. But >> at at East Carolina, didn't play special teams and receive and a returner with your speed, that feels like it could definitely be an option for you at the NFL level. How open are you to that? And is that something that in in whatever conversations you've had with Dallas that they've discussed with you? Yeah, man. I mean, shoot. For me, bro, my goal is to play in the NFL, not just make it. So, whether I get to play a receiver, scout team running back, returner, front line on kickoff, for me it don't really matter, man. I just want to just help the team win and make an impact wherever I can. So, for me, man, I'm open to any and everything, bro. Anthony, talk to me about what the Cowboys are getting from you off the field. What do you like to do in your free time outside of football? What kind of person are you? Shoot, for me, man, I'm a real chill, lax person, man. I got two dogs. So, for me, that's that's where I spend most of my time when I'm not at the facilities or when I'm not doing football. I'm usually outside the dog park or laid up with my pups, man. So, that's that's something that shoot, that that's they've been riding down with me, man, since the NC State days. So, yeah, man. They get all my time when I'm not doing ball, man. What kind of dogs are they? I got a Lab Retriever Hound mix and then I got a Great Pyrenees. Ooh. That's a lot of food, man. Good thing you're getting a contract. Congratulations. >> We we do have a dog food sponsor. So, go ahead and just get on that. >> Oh, definitely. You see me? That might come in handy. >> Yeah, just just keep keep that in mind whenever you get here to Dallas. What are the names? Yeah. Uh, my my girl, her name is Pinto. And then my boy, his name is Prince. We're excited to to see you here in Dallas. Safe travels and we'll talk to you again next week. Yes, sir, man. I appreciate y'all so much for getting on the call, man. See y'all soon, bro. Of course. Thanks, Anthony.

title: 'They fit the culture': Assistant GM Reed Burckhardt evaluates Broncos' 2026 Draft class
text: here with Broncos assistant general manager Reed Birkhart. Reed, the uh 2026 NFL draft just wrapped up and you guys started off with a a flurry of moves at the start of day three. George Payton said yesterday that those first couple of day, excuse me, round four picks could set the tone for this draft. Ended up drafting Jonah Coleman out of Washington, Cage Casey out of Boise State. What' you see with those two guys and and what do they add to this roster? >> What's interesting, he said it was going to set the tone because those are two tone setters. Um Jonah, you know, is a physical downhill runner. fits our style, fits what we have uh in our running back group right now. And then and then Cage is is a physical high makeup, high trait player um that really gonna fit in our old line room and and we talk about setting the tone for our team in the offensive line room and and he certainly is going to add to that. >> Justin Jolie, then you guys trade up to get him. What was it about him that made you guys want to move up the board to add him to this roster? >> Well, fits the theme with with the first two. He's a highly competitive kid. We we really liked our top 30 visit with him. just liked how he carried himself in the building around our coaches, around our staff. Really felt his infectiousness, uh his energy, uh his competitiveness, and he's got a pass game skill set, and so we were really excited to get him because of all those things. >> Sean then mentioned it was a long wait until you guys picked again in round seven, but uh added three guys and Miles Scott, Don Bentley, and then Red Murdoch there with the Mr. Irrelevant pick. What were those final minutes of the draft like as you were able to add three guys who could potentially contribute to this team? Well, when you get to that point, you're hoping they're there, you know, and at that point, everyone's board looks different and so they're coming from from all different angles and and and to get miles um and to add to our safety depth. Uh he was a receiver that converted to to safety and his first year at safety. He started three years started at Illinois and we got a little inside information uh from Palo and and Pat and um man, they were bringing him up to us. He came on a 30 and they were like, "Man, we got to get this guy. We got to get this guy." So, high respect for for those two players and the program they played in and and see that extending with with Miles. And then Don, you know, had a really productive year this year at Utah. Um little bit different play style than Justin. Um a little bit more of an inline wide, bigger body, but um like his upside and then with Red, you know, really productive year at Buffalo. Uh he was ball production, uh forced fumbles, he's always around the ball, special teams upside. So, he's going to fit well in that group as well and really plays to the style that that our defense plays to. >> Re, as you look back on the last three days, I'm not a pick on round one, but you did add Jaylen Wadd to this roster last month. Just how would you evaluate overall this draft class and how it can help this team moving forward? >> Well, I I think the central theme to this draft class is is the things that we touched on with the competitiveness. Uh they fit our culture. all the all these guys, they're going to raise the level uh when they come in and add to our current group and and they're going to fit right in, you know, and so um when we can add to the collective, uh we feel really good about it. >> Reed, appreciate your time and congratulations on another strong draft. >> All right.
