title: General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan & Head Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: [snorts] How's everybody doing? >> Good. How are you? How are you? Did >> you have a good weekend? >> All right. >> What the weekend you guys had? >> Yeah. [laughter] >> Fast and furious. >> What you got? >> Um, how did the draft experience work for you overall? Uh, just the first [snorts] month with you guys together. I would say it was collaborative, cohesive. Um, felt like we executed and I, you know, I think again, like I told you last night, I think we helped the Miami Dolphins. It was, it was a great experience. It really was. Um, we're we're very excited. I think I speak for both both of us when we talk about, you know, the excitement of the the players that we drafted, uh, the culture that we're trying to build. And, uh, you know, number one, they can play. You know, don't don't ever mistake that. We're not going to bring guys in here that we don't think can play on the field, but then when you talk about the wiring of the individuals, we feel like we accomplished what we set out to accomplish. >> Yeah. I mean, I just start off I I think John, Eric, and um that entire staff did an incredible job. Um the work that they put in, the process for me to sit in there for the first time really in a full draft rather than just on one side of the football, it was really cool to see. Um, incredible process, the communication, the collaboration in there, just sticking to all the hard work that they had already done and and watching, you know, the guys kind of fall in place. Um, it was really cool for me to see. Again, I I think he did an unbelievable job in his first draft. Um, very very excited about the players that we picked and I can't wait to coach them. So, just uh cool experience and really excited about the players that we got. >> So, there's this trend. And I think you had four or five sets of college teammates now drafted here. Was that coincidence or is that ever factored into the equation when you're making these picks? >> Purely coincidence, you know, purely coincidence. It's cool. It's a cool story. Um, but no, that there was there there was no agenda or intent there. It just happened. >> Speaking of agendas, it was or no agendas rather. It's hard not to notice that there's one particular state you seem to draw players from. What can you tell us about that? >> Again, um you know, we let the board talk to us and it's the best player available approach and it just again it's coincidence that that we had a lot of guys from the state of Texas this year. Uh they play good football in Texas. So, you know, I think that's probably a good thing, but again, there was nothing that was intentional. It's just the way that it kind of fell. >> How much of a of a priority was physicality in selecting the players? >> Uh it's always a priority. You know, I think we've talked about from the jump just what we're trying to build here, uh, the culture, the competition, and then on top of that, uh, the play style. I'll let him speak to the play style, but I can tell you from the moment that we started working together back in Green Bay, he's he, you know, he says that word or that phrase quite a bit and, uh, and the players adhere to it. Play style and physicality is a big part of what we're trying to accomplish and build here. >> Yeah. I mean, I just, you know, if there's one thing I told him when he asked me my opinion on things, it's one thing I I was not going to back away from. I just I believe this is a physical game and you need tough guys to play this game and guys who want to be physical. And I think if you look at this list and you watch how hard these guys play, I think it's impressive. And what really that that says to me, it's and I've [snorts] said this before, you can find out if a guy loves football based on how hard he plays. you can find out how much a guy loves his teammates based on how hard he plays. And when you look at this, I I think we got the right type of guys and I'm excited to work with them. >> So, you previously talked about the quarterback position um infusing competition into that room, potentially dropping QB every year. Um how close were you to go in QB? Why ultimately decided not to? And where are you on the competition in that room right now? >> Sure. Uh good question. Um I I did say that and it came up a couple times throughout the course of the weekend. Um it just we felt like the better option was the other pick. Um just a chance for for a guy to get on the field and help us this year uh with where we are as a roster. Um but the conversation happened multiple times. Um I you know I'm certainly not backing off what I said initially. We we will take a a quarterback every year, every other year when we have the opportunity. Um, but we just the way that it fell this year. And part of that is we we like our room. You know, we're we're happy with Malik, you know, Quinn is is doing a good job and will continue to do a good job and and we like our number three as well. So, we're we're in good shape there. Uh, and just the way the board fell, it just it didn't work out this year. But, uh, you know, we'll take one next year, if not the year after that. I've got a question about [clears throat] um BPA and conviction and um BPA and conviction I guess over need and I want to see if I have examples correct here. You guys uh took Proctor over Ruben Bane when you needed an edge rusher but BPA and conviction. You take Jacob Rodriguez uh over uh Derek Moore and Zion Young. BPA over conviction and competition. You've got three. You had two starting offensive tackles. You had two starting inside linebackers. Do I am I reading that right? Is that are those examples of BPA and and over and conviction over need? >> Yeah. I mean, and those other guys, again, I want to be I want to make sure I'm being very clear here. You know, those other other guys that you mentioned are very good football players and the Dolphins would have been lucky to have them, but yeah, it is a best player available approach and there's a lot of conversations that go into it. Um, I just you don't you never have any way of knowing what your needs are going to be. You know, I've said that to you before and and I believe that in my heart of hearts. I mean, you can you can have an embarrassment of riches in a room and then you got a hamstring and an ankle and now you're going to your emergency board. So, um, we we took the players that we felt like were the best for the Miami Dolphins. Uh, that's no shot at anybody that didn't end up here. I'm sure they'll go on to have wonderful careers and we wish them nothing but the best, but we're very happy with who we who we took and who we wound up with. >> Was there a point in the draft where you might have considered German McCoy or did you guys have a medically red flag? >> Uh, you know what? I he's a wonderful uh talent and and a really good kid and uh I'm going stay away from talking about the medical of of anybody or any players up here, but uh you know, I wish him the best. I hope he has a great career. >> Can you speak to your process now of adding uh undrafted guys? Um, I guess you can get a handful since you already had 13 draft picks. Uh, and how much of that has already happened? >> Yeah, there it's it's going on as we speak. You know, it's always a fast and furious process postdraft. Um, you know, we have we have our targeted guys and uh and we're in the process of trying to lock those guys up currently. >> About how many might you have room for? >> Uh, it's it's a fluid number. Um, probably I would say eight to 10, you know, just depending on how that goes. One of the more interesting picks I thought was Trayori. The Dolphins have had I hope I pronounced it right. >> Dolphins have had pathway players before, but not drafted pathway players. So, what attracted you to him and how quickly how where do you see him in his development right now? >> Yeah, he's a he's kind of a very raw athletic ball of clay, if you will. Um, he's he can move, you know, he's he's an interesting athlete. He's got twitch, he's got speed, he's got good hands. I think he's a he's a mismatch as a route runner and uh and he should only get better. You know, he hadn't been playing football real long. So, um you know, that that was what was intriguing to us, especially at that value. Uh we felt like a player who's who's ascending and whose best ball is in front of him and uh and can and can be a problem for defenses in time. You know, I have a lot of faith in the coaches who are going to coach him every day to continue to develop him as a pro. Um, but he, you know, he was he was a somebody that we had our eyes on for a while and he fell to us at the right value, so we took a shot. >> Jeff, are there one or two tangible qualities where the Dolphins got better through the draft, whether it's um, you know, competition or speed or size or anything along those lines? >> Well, yeah. I mean, I think we added competition throughout our whole roster and I think that's what you're looking for. I think that brings out the best. And I mean, you could look at all these players and there's different qualities that each of them have and there's different reasons we like some of these players over others. Um, but like we said, competition is going to be the key. Uh, these these 13 players bring that as well as the guys that we have right now on the roster. They'll be here not this week, but the week after, and we'll kind of get them acclimated and then mix a team together, and I'm excited to do that. Do you envision giving Proctor, no matter where he ends up, do you envision giving him looks at guard and tackle on the spring and summer? >> Yeah, for sure. I I think, you know, we we'll sit down and talk, you know, where the best available position for him will be. I think ultimately our job is to get the best five on the field and however that shakes out, um, it's our job to figure that out. um extremely talented player who can do both, which I think is a plus anytime you have versatility in a player. Um I think he can excel at both. We we'll figure out where the best spot is for him, you know, soon as we get on the field. >> Speaking of versatility, you picked a few guys day three and Trey Moore and Kyle Lewis that are kind of viewed as tweeners, right? I'm curious how their versatility um will play a role in your defense. >> That excites me. I think anytime you can draft a player who can do multiple things, it's our job as coaches to have a vision for him and figure out where to play him or play him in multiple spots. What's a down and distance? What's he going to do on early downs? Is he going to be a stack backer on early downs? Is he going to be a sub rusher uh in second, seven plus, third down? Is he a guy that can line up as a spinner and pick guards and rush? Um and then you look at the other guy. Can he can he play outside backer? Can he play inside backer? Can you insert him in different spots on the field? Um, you know, the great part about our conversations is if you find a really good football player, and I mean, smart guy, tough guy, a productive player that jumps out on tape, I think it's our job as coaches to have a vision for him. And then I think it's our job schematically to figure out how to make it work for him. And I think sometimes coaches look at we're playing 34, we're playing 4-3, and he doesn't fit the scheme. I mean, I just I don't agree with that. I mean, let's get the best football players we can and let's figure out what they can do. And now it's going to be fun trying to figure out these guys as we watch them do individual and then we watch them play football to figure out how to make it work. Um, and that excites me as a coach and I've said that before and I think we've got a lot of pieces now to do that. And I just I was sitting there today in the draft meeting. I even showed him I was like drawing up different things different guys can do like that. That's fun for me. And these are really good players that mixed in with the players that we have now. It's our job to go to work and go through the OTAAS and go through training camp and by preeason, you know, we'll see what we can do with them. >> On the same topic on the other side of the ball, you guys added a bunch of players on the O line, tight end that really can play downhill in a foam booth and they have other skills as well, but you also inherit a bunch of guys that have excelled at outside zone scheme. How important was it to you guys to diversify what you can do from a running game scheme standpoint? Well, I think the guys that we have can run outside zone, can run inside zone, and can run gap scheme. I just I think it's the same thing that I just said. Um, the more we can do, the more our players can do, and then let's figure out what they do best and let's go get good at it. >> Jeeoff, we heard Sullie's comments on Chris Johnson, but I want to go back to some things you said about how you scout quarterbacks um at the league meetings. You know, the the three levels of play. when you're watching Chris Shantton play, you know, how did he fare at all three levels? >> No, it's it's it's cool that you remember that. I think he can win at all three and he can take the ball away and he tackles and he's aggressive and I love his play style and he can play inside. I mean, this was one of my favorite guys in the draft that when we started talking about him and it came time to pick him. I mean, I I would not have been surprised if he was taken earlier than we took him. So, he can win at those levels. I'm excited to coach him. He was here yesterday. Um, he's got good size to him. He's got length to him. He's a great person. He loves football. I am very excited to get a chance to coach him. [snorts] When it comes to edge rusher, did you hope to maybe get one in in-house in the first two days? And then how did you feel about coming away with the two you did get here on day three? >> I I just wanted the best player available and I think that's the cool part about this draft and the process and really learning from him and going through this the first time. Um, [clears throat] and it kept coming back to that as we talked. It's do you take this? No, just keep taking the best player you can. and we did that and we stuck to it and I think that will help our team as we go forward. Um and then the other guys that we took really excited about them. I mean guys that have versatility um you know at the end Max has got a toughness to him that we liked. He's a rugged player. He plays really hard. Um and then even like a guy like Trey Moore, right? All the things that Trey can do. The amount of sacks that he's had in his career, the ability to play linebacker, the ability to play off the edge. I mean that's really exciting for us. So, I look forward to seeing those guys and coaching them. >> I think when if I [clears throat] can chime in here, you know, the theme is good football players who can do different things. And as you build a roster, injuries, it's inevitable. Injuries are going to happen. So, it's no different than in life, right? The more you can do, the more value you bring. Um, and that was kind of, you know, that's been our theme all the way through. Let's let's just collect as many really good football players as we can who can do a lot of different things, throw them in the mix, and good things will happen. You know, that that are also I know you guys are tired of hearing me use the phrase wired right, but that are wired right. You know, that that love what they do and are passionate about what they do and have leadership skills and physical and mental toughness. And you're [snorts] not going to go wrong that way. You know, you can win with with with uh with that with that mindset and win with that that process. I believe that my heart of hearts >> and I think you know and I agree with Sully I think what should excite people and what's exciting to us as coaches I mean as I look at these names these are good not only good football players but a they're smart football players they're tough football players it's going to be cool to see this group mixed together u because I think they all have a very similar mindset and I think they all have a little bit of edge to them and that that excites excites me to start coaching. >> Now that you guys have this full picture for the draft class and you try to define the scheme, right, is does it work as starting broad and getting more narrow or is it a matter of starting narrow and then building it out once you kind of get a feel for the guys? >> Well, I think we have right now and you know, Bobby on offense and obviously I have a I'll have a saying that as well and in our defense with Shawn. I mean, we have a um we have a system that we're going to run, but there's tweaks within a system and there's evolutions within a system and there's things that we'll think outside the box to add to the system. But in general, we we've got a really good solid core foundation of the systems that we're going to run that are in place and we've already started teaching to the guys that are here because let's not forget, we've got some we've got some good pieces here already that have been working really hard and doing a really really good job. Um, and we had two really good days of mini camp out there. So, this isn't reinventing an offense or a defense. This is now plugging in players to see who does what best and creating some really really good competition, which that is what excites me the most. Anytime you can add add that, you're going to bring out the best in these guys. >> For an entire secondary that needs to be rebuilt, I mean, you you guys basically partied ways with just about every starter. Why only one quarterback and why one safety? >> We like we like a lot of the guys that we have. Um we've got [clears throat] to spend time with them. We have some guys that were injured last year that are back and we've got to watch them on the field and then um same with some safeties. We brought in some guys. There's guys that were here and you know we did we added obviously we added a safety. We added Chris and then really even getting Kyle who's got the versatility. I know he's listed as a linebacker, but I think you're going to see him move around and do some things back there as well. >> Um, when you guys talk a lot about size, toughness, versatility, the only player that I guess doesn't necessarily Well, I don't want to speak on the toughness part of it because, you know, we'll learn that over time, but I guess size and versatility. Kevin Coleman is the only player that immediately comes to mind that doesn't necessarily fit those. I'm curious what you guys saw out of him. >> Sure. It was just it was an opportunity to add some explosiveness to the offense, some speed, guy that's uh again versatile, can return, you know, help you in the return game. Um, and has been a good player in in in in the most competitive league in college football in the SEC, or at least in my opinion. Uh, and a guy that that we think can can do multiple things. a question. >> All right, guys. >> Thanks, guys. Enjoy your weekend. >> Take care.

title: Eli Heidenreich Introductory Press Conference | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Yeah, I just want to start off uh you know, I think some thank yous are in line. First off, thank you to uh Mr. Rooney, Mr. Khan, and uh Coach McCarthy for, you know, giving me this opportunity and and taking a chance on me. Um and then you I'm thankful for the the coaches back at Navy that have helped get me to this spot. Um Coach Newberry, uh Coach Yokitis, Coach Cole, Coach Kronic. Um and then my family, you know, they they have a big role in why I'm here. Um, so I'm I'm super thankful for my family as well. >> Eli, the Steelers are very touched by that moment there at the end when you were introduced. What was that like for you to walk up through that door? >> Yeah, it was um it was it was pretty incredible. I think you know the biggest thing is is for me I turn that corner and you see the city skyline in the background and then the the crowd is like 90% black and gold. It's all Steelers fans out there and um you know it just it was such a cool moment. Everything kind of just came together and you know I was pretty overwhelmed with the emotions but you know I'm just thankful that I had this opportunity that the NFL invited me to be in the green room and um it just you know allowed for this moment to to be even more special. >> Eli, as the draft was approaching, did you allow yourself the thought of maybe the Steelers are going to take me? So, you know, um I think leading up to the draft, there's always some buzz going around, especially from your agent. He's hearing things from different teams. Um you know, but I I think that buzz was probably the loudest from the Steelers. Uh so I definitely had some sort of inkling coming into uh the draft that the Steelers were interested and I would potentially be drafted by them. Um you know, but you know, time was kind of ticking down at the end and I saw they had one more one more pick. So, you know, I was I was hoping like back of my mind I was like, "Come on." and then the the the call came through and um it was it was pretty cool. So, >> and I know it only happened an hour ago, but has it sunk in yet? >> You know, I don't I don't think fully. I think it's going to take a little bit of time probably to sleep on it and wake up tomorrow morning. Like I'm a Pittsburgh Steeler now. Um I think it, you know, hasn't fully set in. >> Hey, what what can you do for the Steelers as a player? >> Yeah, so you know, I think the biggest thing about me is you're getting a football player. Um, you know, on offense, I can do a lot of different a lot of different things. That's something I've been doing for almost eight years now, high school and college. Uh, playing a few different positions at a high level. So, on the offense side of things, you you're getting some versatility. And then on special teams, I played all four phases um in in college, so I'm able to contribute there and and make a difference. But I think the biggest thing is you look at the Steelers organization um and the mentality that, you know, this this team's been built off. Um, you know, I think I bring that same thing that that toughness, that grittiness that, you know, that not only the the Steelers, but the the city of Pittsburgh has always been about. >> Eli, when you saw the Steelers call you, the 412 number pop up, did you know in that moment that it was the Steelers, or did you think maybe this is like a friend whose number I forgot to say in my phone, something like that? >> Yeah, I had I had um my first thought was definitely Steelers. I saw they were on the clock and I was like, they're like it was just it all kind of hit me at once. Um, yeah, but I thought it was them. Eli, do you remember the the first moment when you dreamed as a kid maybe of playing for the Pittsburgh Steelers? And what was the key to making that dream a reality? >> Yeah, I think the the earliest moment for me that that I can remember is watching the Steelers play the Cardinals in the Super Bowl. Um, and just, you know, watching that game and everything that took place for, you know, us to go out and and win that Super Bowl. I think that was really when it started. Um, you know, I remember James Harrison that play specifically, his 100 yard pick six and, um, you know, I went asked my dad shortly after that for James Harrison jersey, which I got later on that summer. But, so I think then is really when it started. >> What are you looking forward to about being back uh, every day? Obviously, I haven't been too far away, but being back where you're from, what will that be like? >> Yeah, you know, I think the biggest thing that I'm looking forward to um, is really just devoting 100% of my time to football. You know, the last four years I've kind of had this, you know, juggling match of just military and academics and football and just trying to find time for everything. And this is the first time that I'll really have, you know, all of my time to to dedicate to football and I'm excited for that. >> Pittsburgh, as a Pittsburgh guy, what was it like seeing the city kind of transformed by the draft? I mean, could you in all your dreams, could you have imagined seeing the draft stage in front of Back Rusher Stadium and you walking across it? Yeah, I was. It was pretty cool seeing it all take place. Um I'm glad that this city got the publicity for the draft. I think people are finally starting to realize like this city rocks like and more people need to realize that that uh you know what goes down here. Um but just kind of how everything was set up. I think it was just such a fantastic event across the board and I think everything went right. Um and you know for me to be able to go out there and kind of contribute to that and be a part of this event um was really special. >> Go from a zero star recruit >> to now an NFL football player. What were some of the most important things within your journey that that allowed you to achieve this? >> Yep. >> You know, I think you know, like you said, not being super highly recruited. Um, for me it was kind of frustrating initially. Uh, you're like wondering why why am I not getting stars or offers, whatever it may be. But, you know, something my dad really helped me kind of understand is that, you know, use this as a a fuel, a way to motivate you. And I think that taught me how to work. It taught me how to, you know, make myself better on my own accord. Um, so I I think that's the the biggest lesson that I kind of took away from that time is, um, you know, just use it as motivation and, uh, become a better football player as a result. >> Eli, what are your duties now after going to Navy? Now, what does that look like moving forward here? >> Yep. So, uh, May 22nd is my graduation and I'll commission into the reserves in the United States Marine Corps. Um, and all of my, uh, you know, time and focus will be on football. I won't have any military obligations taking me away from football. Um they may ask me to do some sort of like PR related event in the offseason to shine light on the Marine Corps or the the military, but that's um kind of all all I have to do. Um and then afterwards, I'll have the choice to go back and serve in an active role. But um as uh as as far as I'm concerned right now, you know, I'm worried about being a Steeler. >> Eli, is there a Steeler or non-Steeler past or present that you modeled your game after? Um, you know, I've I've always looked up to Chris McCaffrey, I think he's a just a fantastic player and plays the game the right way. And, you know, as a as watching him and and the way, especially in the past game, the way he's able to get open and and make things happen in space, uh, is something that I've always, you know, tried to study and and replicate. >> What was your journey at the Naval Academy like? >> Um, man, it was tough some days and I mean that that's done on purpose. You know, it's um it's designed to be stressful. They want you to have to operate in a stressful environment and get used to that. Um, but you know, I'm thankful for those those tough times. You know, there there were some long nights there and you got a lot on your plate. Um, but it it just teaches you how to, you know, deal with that stress and uh to really time management, be able to plan out your your days and weeks in a time that makes sense for you. Um, but yeah, the the the academy is tough sometimes, but I'm glad I went through that struggle. I think it made me a better person. Was that preparing you for days like today or do you still get nervous as you're waiting to hear your name go? >> I was definitely definitely nervous. My heart was, you know, my heart rate is probably a little elevated today. I would say more so than usual, but um sitting on sitting on a couch isn't too bad compared to what we got to do on a day-to-day basis there. So, >> you mentioned want to get a James Harrison jersey. He was around this weekend. Did you get to talk to him, see him, anything like that? >> I did not have the chance, but um I would love to sometime. It' be pretty cool. Do >> you still have that jersey? I'd have to check. I I would assume so. I I did not get rid of it. It'd be something like my my parents would be like, he doesn't it doesn't fit him anymore. But yeah, you know, kind of reflecting back on your 2021 state title run with Mount Lemon. Um how did that kind of grow your football career and and what did that teach you, especially to do it alongside a guy like Alex Tesco who then became obviously your teammate? >> Yeah, it's funny you ask. Um you know, you look at that Mount Lebanon team. Um we're just we're a normal public school. there's no recruiting going on. I've been playing that senior class I played with that year. I've been playing with literally my entire life since like first grade. Um and we we played football throughout, you know, growing up and then that senior year we just happened to be really good. And I think that was the result of us playing so long together and getting to know each other and, you know, kind of having this love for each other, this like brotherly love. Um, you know, I think that really taught me that, you know, an important part of any football team is that, you know, connection you have to your teammates and making sure that you're looking out for them. And the same thing goes at Navy. There's no NIL or anything like that. It's just, you know, you're you're worried about your your brothers to the left and right of you. So, that's something I took away from that. >> Did you go to games growing up or did you ever go to a training camp or anything like that >> for the Steelers? Yeah, I went to a bunch. the mo I was at the game that we beat the Ravens and they missed the field goal like in December. So that was the most recent game. I went to the playoff game last year in Baltimore. Definitely got chirped a little bit. I was full Steelered up. Um but uh yeah, I've been to a ton, you know, growing up and then even recently >> wear jerseys now still like >> if I'm going to a game I will. But um >> players in your collection or >> so I snatched my dad's old Paul Malo jersey and I have my dad had an old Rod Woodson jersey too that I'll throw on here here and there. So >> you know just for clarification you talk about going in and being a reserveist while you are like do you have any kind of obligations in terms of like an annual training or anything like that? >> Sorry. Can you repeat that? >> Like as a reserveist will you have any obligations with like annual training or anything like that? As far as I'm concerned, no. Uh I've been talking with Rayon Lane. He's a safety in uh Jacksonville who got drafted out of Navy last year and um you know, he he hasn't had to deal with any of that. The only thing he'll have to do, like I said, was that PR kind of a few things in the offseason, but nothing significant. Nothing in season. >> Eli, how does your military physical training prepare you for football training? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I think the biggest thing, uh, you train for in the military is just, you know, conditioning. Um, being able to operate at a real long time. And, um, that's something that we definitely do in the the academy offense. We try to wear you down throughout the game. Um, so I'd say, you know, that that conditioning is something that I've worked on throughout my career and something that I do well. >> How are you going to spend the rest of tonight and what does, uh, the next couple weeks look like for you until rookie mini camp? >> Yeah, so I live about 15 20 minutes from here. Um, I have a bunch of family and friends at my house and then like 20 of my Naval Academy football teammates drove up for the weekend. So, we had a little convoy coming in after class Friday. Um, but they're all they're all waiting back at the uh at the house and you know, I'm I'm going to go hang out with them. >> Two more questions. >> Is that 71? >> It is. Yep. >> What's it been like being around Ravens fans for the past 3, four years? >> It's uh it's it's pretty rough sometimes. There's there's a lot at the academy, too, since it's in Maryland. It's pretty close proximity to uh to Baltimore, so you're definitely around them. Um but yeah, it's uh you just have to, you know, close your ears sometimes. >> Thank you, Eli. Thanks for your service. >> Thank you guys.

You know, the the time and effort they put into this. You know, we haven't done this in what, 19 years with the new staff here and the way these guys uh just work so hard. So, from there, happy to take any questions. Omar, was the um offensive heavy draft was that kind of reflective of having Mike in his background? What what you want to do on offense or Sure. >> No. Uh he uh you know, it just sort of came that way. Yeah, you know, when when you're the draft happens, there's a lot of excitement that goes on to in and um you know, there was no ill intent and you know, made the call, but um as I mentioned, when you have a a good process and you trust your board and you know, the draft throws curve balls at you and and every round, trust me, it happens throughout the throughout the draft and some public, some not. And um you know, things just sort of take care of themselves. after taking a swing at a receiver there initially at 21, how do you feel you guys pivoted to address that position? And Mike, how do you feel your room is now after batting the guys that you did today? >> Well, I think Omar's really has answered the question. Um, you have to trust your board. I've always looked at the draft board similar, you know, to calling a a huge game, you know, but obviously with a lot more energy in it. I mean, there's so much time and energy goes into putting that board together and it's this draft this weekend was very refreshing when you see need hit value. When value hits need and so when you when you get down to those picks, you know, you're usually talking about two, three, four players and um but it really did it, you know, we did not go into the draft saying we're going to take so many offensive players or so many defensive players. we wanted to raise the level, you know, of our of our talent and we're we're aware of positions that we would probably want to add to, but um you know, and that's the case with receiver. I mean, it's just I mean, he was he was right there and um that's that's a great pick pick right there. >> Did you Bernard and um the kick returner from Iowa feel? >> We got what >> how did you feel about the room after you got Bernard in the second round? >> Yeah, I mean we we feel you know obviously we traded up to get Jeremy. So, uh, I think that kind of speaks for how we feel about him. Um, you know, we think he's going to add to the room. And then Kaden, you know, that's that's on coach. He's going to have some fun with him, I think. And, uh, you know, obviously his his, uh, he's going to help us in the return game, which was a area need for us. >> Adding, uh, Drew Aller in the third round, what kind of value do you feel like you got with him and what are you getting and that made him the attractive pick? >> I mean, it's about the quarterback room. Uh, I've always approached it that way. I I learned it that way as a as a young coach. Um it's it's about training the whole room together and we you know we had an opportunity to get on the field last week uh for two days, you know, with Mason and and Will and and now we had Drew. So this this is this is this is the goal. This is the outlook. I mean, we talked about it in my interview just from a philosophical standpoint. So we we want to have a healthy, you know, quarterback room that that we're always developing. We're always developing it. It's the most important position maybe in sports. I mean, it's very difficult. There's a lot that goes into that. Uh we have a way of how the quarterback will be trained here. Uh I've done it a long time and um it's great to have two really young guys that I'm I'm extremely excited about. >> Does drafting Drew affect what you guys expect to hear from Aaron or what you want to hear from Aaron? >> It was it's No, not at all. This is uh this is about developing the room and trying to make the room as deep, you know, as we possibly can. >> If you if you do get an answer from Aaron who does decide to come here, would you be comfortable with two guys who haven't taken a snap in the NFL as backups or would you need to to keep Mason to give yourselves another guy? >> I mean, these are all questions, answers, hypotheticals that really it won't change what I've already said. I will I will coach the hell out of that room. Um, I have a lot of confidence. I have history and experience that that um, you know, I will give everything I I can to any quarterback in that room. So, we we we want to grow the quarterback room. We we don't want to, you know, just rely on one quarterback. >> AFC North in terms of the size, the arm strength, the hands. Is he the AFC North quarterback we've been talking about for a while now? >> Well, I I think the biggest thing is you recognize where you play. I mean, you you know, you're going to have eight home games. So, u it's no different with the return game. You know, the return game is is was a very important, you know, outlook uh for for Omar and I from the first day we start talking about the draft. >> What did it be like by Drew Waller? And um was he the guy you wanted on day two? >> Definitely. I mean, uh I I think like anything, you know, I I believe in first impressions. you know, I've had a chance to to have, you know, watch him play, but meet meet him at the combine. Um, and really all the quarterbacks that came into the meeting room there did very well. But I I just, you know, I liked everything about him. I think he's I think he's young. I think he's got a lot of great, you know, a lot of room for growth and and, you know, he's a young man that can throw the ball with the best of them and that that that's a great starting point to have. Mike, one of the challenges in having two young quarterbacks and giving them time to be able to develop. >> CBA rules is the only challenge we have, but um you know, everybody coaches under him, but it's it's a good place to be. Um you know, I was very impressed with Will last week. You know, I knew he was a good athlete. Um you know, we had a chance Tom and I had a chance to break down. We do a thing called quarterback profile. So, we had the chance to videotape that on Tuesday and and that's something we'll share, you know, with Mason and and Will on Monday. But, you know, it's there's a training regimen that's involved. Um, but, you know, we'll stick to it and um I'm I'm excited about both those guys. >> How about roster rules too, Omar? Like you'd said, Mike, on Monday, you'd like to have four and use the practice squad the right way. How what are the minations that you can kind of use to your advantage to try to hold on to four >> four quarterbacks >> practice squad? Like how do you how do you do that? >> Yeah. I mean those are all you talking about once we get into the season. >> Yeah. >> Yeah. I mean those are all options. You know the one thing about this league is you know there's natural attrition that happens uh once you get into training camp and injuries happen and that sort of sorts itself out. But you know the league's set up where you have uh options and opportunities to keep your best players. >> Mike, have you ever had a service academy guy and Hiden specifically? How do you envision >> I'm sorry I didn't hear the first part of that. >> Have you ever had a service academy guy and how do you envision Hiden being used? Oh, I I think the biggest thing is um you know, obviously have a lot of respect for for what what he's done the last four years. Um we we talk a lot about how many downs a player plays. You know, does he play all four downs? You know, his ability to play multiple positions. So, I think Eli definitely brings that to the table. So, um I think both, you know, we I just I met with uh Angelico briefly, you know, earlier. So, I I think we're going to open up our playbook a little bit. Mark mentioned the emotion that came with drafting Eli and you know the crowd going crazy for you. What is that moment like to draft a Pittsburgh native guy and see him get to walk across the stage in front of this Pittsburgh crowd? >> Oh, I mean I I think everybody in the room felt it. I felt it. Um I I couldn't imagine what it would you know what it been to walk out there like that. So just really proud of him and you know and I think the biggest thing for me as a coach is to create opportunities for for all these guys and especially for Eli. more bigger picture just um when you enter the draft with 12 draft picks that's a lot of capital. What was your plan to try to leverage that to your advantage and how do you feel like you executed it? >> Um I think the execution went um went pretty good. You know, really really happy with how with the players that we acquired. Um you know, we went into I mentioned to you guys, I didn't know if we were going to end up with 10 or 14 picks. You know, we were open to anything. There was some good players in the draft. It there really was. And uh you know, we got 10 good ones. And um you know, I'd like to tell you that I went in there saying, "Hey, we're going to end up with 10 or end up with nine or eight and four first rounders, but you know, you just sort of have to let it come come to you and uh you trust your process." >> When you talk to player like Kaden whose contributions have primarily come on special teams, how do you try to balance the value that that provides compared to maybe a depth at another position or a guy who could be a potential future starter in >> Yeah, I mean I think his resume speaks for itself, you know. Um he's very productive in that area in college. I mean that's that's I mean just just look at his stats. I mean I think that speaks for itself. But you know it was a neat position. Um he was the top guy in that area in my opinion. Um and uh you know for us that's the value we we we put on him and we we feel really good about where we got him. >> Max is it a case where since he took up football so late do you see a higher ceiling that there's still ascension in terms of where his game can be or he learns more even? >> Oh absolutely. Absolutely. I mean, he he's so impressive. I mean, you guys got to meet him got to meet him uh yesterday and uh I mean, there's there's a lot to like there and a lot of growth to come and you know, I'm excited for him being a Pittsburgh Steeler for years and years to come. >> I know Mike was giving you grief about it, but how did the 8minute clock thing come into play and was was that at all an issue with the whole thing with Mai? Were you like did you have time to go back to the Cowboys and say, >> "Hey, you know, can we get can we can we swing something here?" Yeah, it was it was a non-issue. I probably made more out of it than I I I should have the other day, but it it was fine. >> You first impressions earlier. What were your first impressions of Jennings Dunkerk? He's a seems like a pretty interesting guy and uh would stand out even in a crowd of 10 offensive linemen, I think, when you look at him. >> Yeah, I mean, we love his hair. I mean, we're we're it's, you know, I'm sure our marketing marketing department likes it even more, but no, he's impressive. Uh I know James Camp and and and the whole offensive line staff. I mean just you know so impressed with him and I think it's just like anything when you you sit there and watch these men whether you do a zoom or meet him in person you go through the you know the process first time you you may meet him is at the combine but he's you know when he walked through the door I mean he's he's a very very impressive young man. >> What stood out to you guys about Gabriel Rubio? >> Sorry. >> Well I just think number one you watch the way he plays and you look at you look at his skill set. I mean, he's he's a he's a Pittsburgh Steeler defensive lineman. I think he's an outstanding fit for the 34 and I thought that was a no-brainer pick right there. >> Why is fullback still important in your offense and when your thoughts on Riley? >> Well, Rally, I think when you look at Rally, his versatility just jumps off the charts. I mean, if you go back through his background at Wisconsin, you know, he played in the two back offense, played in the three surface offense where he played, you know, both the fullback up on the line, did all the movement ability. You know, he played one year in a in a run and shoot type one back. So, he has some he has some one back running ability, too. And and I cannot, you know, tell you how impressed I was with him and his story uh to leave Wisconsin and to go to Indiana and be a captain on the national championship team. So, um, this is an outstanding pick and and on top of that, I know I'm excited about it cuz I I love the two back offense. There's a lot of things that, um, you know, you you start in this league in the '9s where, you know, two back offense was a primary component of normal down in distance. Now, to be able to bring some of that back, it's something that did a little bit in Dallas, you know, down there to, you know, 23 and 24. So, to be able to have that, but the big part of it, no one's happier than Danny Crossman. I mean, you know, he's a fourcore special tamer. You know, he'll have a chance to potentially be a leader captain type on special teams. So, uh, I thought that was an excellent pick there by Omar. >> Mike, on the offensive line, you have a lot of youth, a lot of positional flexibility, and then also the question mark's health. How you go about sorting out where all these moving pieces fit together? >> Great question. Uh, there's different ways of doing it. You know, I've done left side, I've done right side. I think you got to look at the experience of these guys, how we bring these rookies into the into the into the place. So, um, those discussions have started. Um, and frankly, until we sit down with the players, you know, I'm not going to sit here and talk about it openly until then. But yes, it's I mean, because you you want to create an opportunity for everybody to have a chance to line up. But, boy, the longer I do this, it takes it takes the whole group to get through get through the season. So how we train them together in their in their position flex will be will be a big part of our decisions on how we start. >> Omar, you ended up drafting a lot of guys that were younger but also had multi-year experience. Was that kind of a concentrated effort to get guys that had multiple years of starting but also I think were 23 or younger. I think the only guy that's 23 or older was Oian out of your picks. >> Yeah. You know what it's goes back to you just kind of trust your board. We didn't go into it saying, you know, we want to average this age group by the end of the or this amount of experience. It just it just sort of and we trusted our board and it came to us that way. >> I appreciate your question cuz I I didn't realize that. >> Yeah. Until >> you said it. Yeah. >> It's good homework. >> Two more two more guys. When you get to that stage, you got 200 lb guy that runs a 43. Is that something that you just look at the that skill set in terms of the safety you talk the first the first time around pick? >> Yeah. Yeah. >> That that size, size, and speed. >> Yeah. size and speed, you know, value at that at that spot. Our scouts really liked him. Um, just, you know, special teams contributor. Um, a lot to like there. >> Is Eli is Eli a running back who catches the ball or is he more of a receiver? How what's how do you use him? You said to open the playbook, >> definitely no position flex. I mean I mean he can play from the slot, he can play from the back field. You know, you see him out displaced. Uh, you know, I think anything when you you put a young man in the receiver room, he has to play all three positions. that's the way we want to play. That's the way it's been introduced the last couple weeks. Uh but his ability also to play from the back field and you know just you know the diversity is is is important. So like I said um you can't do everything Randle Cobb you know I've had different players in the past. So we'll definitely look at those things. >> All right. Hey guys, I I meant to mention one thing when I in my intro. Um she's gonna not be happy with it, but Moren Manion, you know, our assistant, she's she's retiring and uh she's been here since uh my first day in 2001 and she's very special to all of us down there and you know, I just, you know, she's probably not be happy with what I said this guys, but I just want to publicly say, you know, how much we're going to miss her and appreciate uh all her all of her her hard work through the years. She's been a a great asset for us and uh we're going to miss her. So, if you guys get a chance to see her, if I know some of you guys know her, just please congratulate her. So, >> all right. Thank you. >> She's she's a manion. I played for her uncle, so she's right stuff.

title: Mike Borgonzi Recaps the 2026 NFL Draft | Press Conference
text: Wrapped up today, uh with five more picks. Um and um you know, first I want to thank the uh everybody in the organization for the past few days here. Uh it's really more than 3 days. I mean, this it's an entire year. Uh especially with our scouts, all the time that they put in on the road, away from their families. Um you know, they are really the lifeblood here um scouting these players and um you know, all the people in the building, our our department, uh the personnel department, uh the coaches that put so much time and energy into um into evaluating these guys and communication I thought was was really good uh between between the personnel department and the coaching. Um and then just our entire support staff, our medical, um you know, when we bring these guys in on 30 visits, it's uh there's a lot of different touch points with everybody in the building. Um you know, strength coaches, trainers, um our dieticians, um um Ev sits down with them, too. Um he'll give us his evaluation. So, um there's there's so much time that's put into it for these 3 days, but uh I really appreciate all the work that uh that they've given us here. Um so. Mike, uh day three picks a lot of times don't come in immediately and contribute on offense or defense, but do special teams, but given that you have you want to create competition on the offensive line, how quickly do you feel like Kube and Carmona can get in that mix and have a chance to start? Yeah, I mean, listen, these guys have played a lot of football, both of them. Um and um they they really do fit the definition of always say like the tough, smart, dependable. I mean, they are they epitomize it. Those two guys. Um and they've um like I said, they've had a lot of snaps there in college football. Um and um they're physically, you know, where they're at right now, the size. Um I think they can come right in here and and and compete. How much do you think that experience >> [clears throat] >> maybe not necessarily make up for what what they may lack athletically, but benefit them as far as, you know, getting them in here and getting ready to compete right away? Yeah, I think there's a maturation to it, especially with the old lineman. Um that uh you know, they've played so much and um and you know, they've they've been around, you know, probably a lot of different coaches. Um you know, both guys had um you know, uh Fernando was um at uh San Jose State, went to Arkansas. And then with Pat, was at Notre Dame and then finished his uh his season for your national champs. Um and um yeah, so they they played a lot of football, so I think that does help, Buck. Can you give a a cliff notes version, maybe on the on your five today, just their strengths, what they're about? Yeah, I mean, I'll hit uh Fernando first. I mean, that like I just said, the the the intangibles part with these guys. Um you know, they're gritty. Um you know, we have these these alpha tags uh for leadership for for these offensive lineman. And and um both him and Pat both have that. Um and Fernando played left tackle um you know, at uh San Jose State, played some tackle in '24 at Arkansas and then played guard and then also has the capability of playing center, too. Just really hadn't done it much in a game. They've done it in practice before. Um with Pat, you know, Pat has obviously played center at Indiana uh this past year. Um I've never seen a guy get an MVP um as an offensive lineman in the Rose Bowl. Uh it just speaks to, you know, the type of player he was uh there for them, uh the leadership. And Pat's also played some guard at um at Notre Dame as well. How about your other guys? Um Yeah, so with Nick, I mean, Nick was a highly productive uh running back at Penn State, played played played a lot of snaps there, too. He was a basically started there 4 years. Um it's funny, I remember turning on the film, I forget who I was watching at Penn State a couple years ago, it might have been two, three years ago, and I see this number 10 and he runs really angry and he's fast and he can catch the ball and we had a there was a guy we had in Kansas City, Pacheco, kind of reminded me of him a little bit. Um so I've I've been feel like I've been watching him for a long time. Um and then with with Jaren, you know, he was really interesting because um you talk about an athlete. I mean, the guy was a a linebacker for 3 years and then he didn't play tight end, you know, and then picked it up and uh he's you know, he's played H-back, he's moved around, he's kind of played fullback a little bit. Um you know, really athletic, really good special teams player. Um so he's going to I think contribute there right away on teams. You had Jackie, too. Yeah, and Jackie I'm sorry, Jackie, too. Yeah, Jackie um you know, the the first time you saw him, I kind of watched a little bit of him at Baylor last year. Um you know, he's playing five technique, he's playing three technique, so I think he's versatile. Um he's explosive on contact, he's twitchy. Um and you know, we see him here, he can probably play a little big end, but mostly, you know, inside as a DT for us. Um coach Aaron Weinkauf actually had him at the East-West um when he coached in that game. Um and our scouts got to visit with them there. Um and then Aaron actually was at his pro day and worked him out, too. So, we've had a lot of different touch points with him. Staying with the offensive lineman, you talked as far back at least as the at the owners meetings to us about being able to sacrifice some some traits and get that toughness and and and play with that. What do you lose when you don't have, you know, the prime athleticism there and how does a line maybe function fine without that? You know, sometimes with these guys, but that's a good question because, you know, the toughness part always shows up. That's the intangibles part. They're usually strong, they're tough, they're smart. Um and sometimes they're so smart, sometimes they know some of their limitations as well. Uh they're so technically sound. Um so, you know, um when you have some of these guys playing next to each other, they're kind of the same way. Um they they make up sometimes for, you know, whatever limitations they might have um you know, with their toughness and and their technique and fundamentals. If you're slotting Jackson right now, you have him at center or guard? Um right now, obviously with the new staff, he's he's playing both. He's going back and forth between guard and center. Um you know, he's played probably more guard primarily right now, but uh but he also has some center snaps and and those guys will be interchangeable here throughout OTAs and training camp, too. With uh with Singleton, first off, what did the eval tell you about the injury? How quick do you think he can be back? And then two, does he add something to the running back room, a trait that maybe you guys didn't have that you were kind of looking to fill? Um you know, I think he's a he's a bigger back. Um he's probably a little bit you know, he's a little bigger than Tony. Um and um you know, the speed, he actually catches the ball really well out of the backfield, too. Um and as far as the injury, uh he's um you know, he should he should be you know, I don't put a timetable, but you know, when he comes in here, we'll tell you, look, but you know, he's he'll be participating here in the spring. Are you going to cut some people now in order to have a bigger undrafted class? You're not going to keep yourself to four guys here, are you? Yeah, those are the things we're working on here throughout the week. Um you know, tonight and and really throughout the week. Um cuz technically, all these guys, I know you might hear some stuff on Twitter and all that stuff and um none of these guys can really be signed until they they walk in the building. Do you expect to have a regular-sized class opening? Um we'll see how it shakes out. Yeah. What's the schedule for these guys? When how soon will they be back here? Uh they'll be back today, Sunday, uh what, the end of the week? Yeah. Yeah. Mike, with with this draft, do you feel that uh you kind of you know, a lot of talk about best player available at spots, but you have holes on this roster. Do you feel that you may have taken a good step with this class to try try and fill those spots? I do. I mean, I think that's the the goal. I mean, obviously you want to take the best player, but you try to marry up um value with need. Um there's there's a part of that. Um without reaching for the need. And that's why I always say like just take the best player. Let's not just reach for a guy just cuz we need, but but I do think we we we did um we did fill some needs. Yeah. Anything else? This is Mike, does the does the UDFA like how you how you target the UDFAs? Does that kind of fill in the holes that maybe you feel like you missed or is it are those guys that kind of just add value to the current draft class? Yeah, I I think it's an extension of really the draft class, you know, but we I wish we could have 20 picks sometimes, but No, you didn't. I know. What do you got, Paul? Um I know you did a lot of work at at defensive back in free agency and everything. This is just the third time in the history of the franchise in Nashville that the draft hasn't included defensive back. What's it say about where you are with Marcus Harris and Tony Adams? And I know the early indications are it's maybe a focus for you with undrafted. Um yeah, I mean, obviously we we added um you know, Flott and Alontae, too. Um you know, to come in here and start. So, um and then having Marcus back and signed Tony, as well. So, um well, it like even when the draft is over, it doesn't, you know, we're still working here on trying to improve the roster. It's never going to stop, whether it's waiver claims, tryouts, um you know, it it doesn't stop. So, um we're going to continue with every position to to to keep working, try to get the best 53 by start of the season. You you talked about [snorts] coach Mack, I guess at your pre-draft press conference. What was it like to see maybe everybody in that war room wearing the coach Mack shirts today and then the people across the league kind of honoring him as well? Yeah, you know, I thought it was it was it was it was a great tribute uh to him and how many people he um he really had an impact on the league. Um and you know, the more you find out uh I mean, he knew everybody throughout the week, it seems like. Um so, I thought it was really special to see um you know, to see us wear these shirts here today and um and and some of the pins that you know, everybody was wearing throughout the draft. It was a a great tribute to him. All right. Thank you, everyone. >> Okay, appreciate it.

title: Jaren Kanak Talks About Joining the Tennessee Titans | Press Conference
text: Jaren, congratulations on being chosen by the Titans. What went into the whole process of switching from linebacker to tight end last year for the Sooners? Yeah, definitely. So, I I grew up my entire life I was an offensive player and it was it was kind of just coming out I was I was recruited at the college level as more of a defensive, you know, style player and that's what I did my first 3 years, but you know, I kind of got to a position in my career in my junior year of college where I kind of realized that that maybe defense wasn't for me and I I basically just approached coaches in the off-season and said, "Hey, listen, I got the offensive background. I'm kind of hitting a wall in my career here on defense and you know, I really think I might be able to offer more to this team if if you let me try out offense." You know, I was just I was just trying to find a place where I could add value to the team and you know, be a guy that was able to lead us towards success. So, they gave me the opportunity to switch over in the spring. They gave me a spring to try it out and you know, it ended up working out pretty well for me. As far as your mentality on the defensive side of the ball, taking that to offense, what all did you kind of take over there to that side of the ball when you were moved there? Yeah, I mean, obviously playing linebacker you kind of have a a little bit of an edge to you. There's a little more tenacity there. Obviously, you play the the game in an aggressive style manner and that that's something I like to do. Jaren, you said you hit a wall as a defensive player and that you, you know, mentioning your offensive background, you played quarterback in high school. How did that help you make that transition to tight end and how do you feel like that's, you know, going to help you as you transition to the NFL level? Yeah, definitely. You said obviously playing quarterback you have a very, you know, holistic understanding of of what goes on in an offense, an offensive scheme and then having that defensive background as well in the in the system that I was in with Coach Brent Venables. It was a very holistic system as well where you you needed understanding of everything that was going on around you and to to make everything work. And so, having having that that that mindset and understanding of the whole concept of of any given play is is really going to help me moving forward. And it has really helped me. What was this whole process like for you, kind of getting ready for the draft, waiting for it today and then kind of getting the call that you're getting picked? Yeah, definitely. I mean, obviously just just the draft process in the spring, you know, a pro day, combine, all that stuff. I was just I felt incredibly blessed to be in the position to go through all that and then obviously getting getting to draft day, there's there's a lot of a lot of different emotions going through the day and you know, getting here towards the later rounds is it's a crazy thing, but I'm I'm I'm glad that I ended up where I did and and I'm happy to call myself a Titan. What role do you see yourself fitting in at your size and your speed, athleticism profile in the NFL and what have the Titans kind of told you about the ways they want to use you? Yeah, definitely. So, I I plan on walking in day one and making an immediate impact on on special teams in particular. You know what I mean? Just Just with my my linebacker background and my athletic ability and understanding of of you know, the game of football and being able to use my athletic abilities to my advantage. I'm I'm looking to be a big contributor on special teams and then, you know, carving out a role for myself within the offense, you know, being a a playmaker in that sense. Where'd you grab the hat and how anxious are you to get one with the new logo on it? Is this the old logo? Oh, it is, right. Okay, so I guess we did like a a mass order on Amazon. So, I need to get one with the the new logo. So, I'm rocking the old one for now. So, you said you did a mass order, you got all 32 teams and then that's that's the Titans one you got? Yes, sir. This is the one that came with it. What can you tell us maybe which I know you lost your dad when you were young. Can you tell us what you remember about him, switching to wear his number and honor him in school as well? Yeah, definitely. So, obviously my my dad passed away when I was when I was younger. So, I have I have very limited memories of of him personally, but just growing up and hearing the way that my family and people around him talked about him and and how he lived his life was just was just something that I wanted to, you know, model my life after and you know, they've had nothing nothing but good things to say about who he was as a man and how much he appreciated and enjoyed and and made people around him better. You know, I've just kind of just taken that and tried to lead my life through that same example.

title: Seahawks Draft Day 3 Press Conference: John Schneider & Mike Macdonald Recap The 2026 NFL Draft
