title: Rob McCartney Highlights The Bucs 2026 Draft Class | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: What's up? Are we good? Are we good? You got rid of that seventh round pick. >> Yeah, thank you. Like no other. >> He's very attentive. I was thinking I'd see you guys in about two or three hours, but now I'm ready to go. Um >> Like no other. No doubt. I got a lot of names in my head from players, uh but also first want to thank everybody like we've made a tradition here recently. So, I'll start with all the college scouts. Tony Hardy, Byron Kiefer, Andy Spier, Brian McLaughlin, Cesar Rivera, Zack Smith, Emmett Clifford, Corey Finney, Jeremiah Bogan, and Jordan Merrell. We got some first-timers in there, too. So, these guys did a great job. Tony Hardy's really answered the bell as our college director for these guys. Um always laugh it's not their Super Bowl. Our Super Bowl is the Super Bowl, but this is a big day for all of us, especially those uh group of college scouts that put a lot of work into this. So, definitely want to take the time to mention them all. Uh Sean Connolly, Donovan Cotton, and Shannon Hogue in our pro department do a tremendous job getting us prepped for all the team needs, chipping in on 30 visits, chipping in um with some of the evals, too. So, shoutout to all them as well. Peyton Roth, our scouting coordinator, Sheldon Quarles, um and then Griffin Moore, our new scouting assistant along with Ty Schiffler. First go-round for those two, they were great. And then just all the travel that we have for all the prospects coming in, our travel throughout the fall, combine travel, Senior Bowl, uh Peyton and Sheldon do a tremendous job with that. Uh Spencer Dill, Joey Larow, and our recent hire Justin in our football IT department. Um and then Zach Beasline who came on with us last year has just been an integral asset to all of us everything that we do. And then real quick, player engagement for all the visits and interviews, Duke, Tyler Massey, Tim, Zach, Miranda in ops for all their help, video guys for all the pro days, all the film, Brett, Matt, RJ, Levi, and Justin, our medical crew, all the doctors who do such a great job giving us all the information we need, including Bobby, Dutchy, John, Sam, and Mel. And then our nutrition staff we're going to add in this year, we had a huge spread upstairs, it was insane, way too much food, but we're all very well fed and now very happy after all those picks. So, thank you to Jess, Pat, and staff as well. And lastly, the people I have spent more time with than my family lately, obviously Jackie Greenie, um shoutout to Greenie, we did two trades this year, he executed zero of them. So, we can hold that over his head a little bit. And then Shane, uh Mike Beel, and then obviously Jason for just uh empowering all of us. He's he's really the best. So, with that, open up for questions. We had four picks, and then we're going to add about 15 guys here in a minute. So, um fired up. Awesome day. So, just on the macro, like the the whole draft, um you you obviously weigh in on this trying to find the best players, right? >> Sure. Um and and obviously you had certain needs that lined up great with Yep. with so many of them being and others. But, >> [snorts] >> it seems like all these guys not coincidentally have a bit of an edge. >> Yeah, for sure. You feel like that was a mission accomplished? And and what how much better did you get in that area this year? >> Yeah, I think obviously it was a point of emphasis for us. It's something we've always talked about, but definitely more of a enhanced focus on that this offseason. Um again, something we've always talked about, but just um it's funny after we drafted Trotter, we're sitting up there and we're talking about teams running the ball against us, just the physicality of having A'Shawn, um having Reuben, and then having Trotter. So, just some of the things that that may limit opposing defenses to be able to do. And then throughout the whole draft, just the energy um and the pride that all these guys really show on the field is, you know, that's really what all the eye in the man stuff starts with. It's a football character thing, but really like when you watch them, you should want to feel their energy, feel their passion for the game. And I think that's something that we always try to knock out of the park, but feel pretty good about that with this class. And to that effect, I mean, you look at these picks, you talk about like Scott today. these guys are are guys that it it seems like you're in a much better position to be able to stop the run, to get back to doing that. I mean, was that something that you guys were really intentional about this draft? >> yeah, I mean, always an emphasis for us. I mean, that's, you know, I think we all believe even though this has become a true passing league, but if you can't stop the run, then you're going to have a long day at the office. So, I think being able to do that, setting up uh you know, more third and longs this year, getting us into more advantageous down and distance to be able to get after the quarterback a little bit and and and in some more different ways. So, but I mean, those guys, I mean, K Scott's a pretty good blitzer, he's a pretty good cover player, too. And um [snorts] I think Key Part's going to be probably a better rusher at this level. Not saying that's the reason we drafted him, but I think we can unleash him a little bit more. Um so, and Trotter's a really good blitzer as well, too. So, I think he's got a lot of assets to him in the pass game as far as coming after the quarterback, too. So, like all those guys for all those reasons. But yeah, I mean, I think we're really excited about the physicality that we've added on all sides of the ball. When you look at the the first-round pick and the second-round pick, that's your top edge rusher Yep. that you needed. And you have a new Mike linebacker. >> Yep. Both these guys are 21 years old. And they could be here for a long time. You know, that's that's what the hope is, right? For you guys to have that two guys come in like that, around the same age, that have a a really long runway to to improve and and help this franchise for a long time. How how how key is that? I know you weren't planning on that, but I mean, but that's what happened. Yeah, I think when we realized, um you know, top of the second round that there was a chance to be able to do that, like the synergy of having a young edge rusher and a young Mike to come in and really kind of become the identity of our defense is really, you know, that's two of the more important spots on defense, and I think we're really excited to have that youth be able to picture those guys, hopefully, you know, it's a year-to-year league, and it's hard to look past those two and three years sometimes, but to be able to say like, "Hey, like we may have these guys for, you know, I think Jason said to one of the guys on the phone, "What are you doing for the next 5 to 10 years?" So, hopefully we're able to, you know, see that through with all of them being in being in Tampa. Rob, is it cool you guys were probably hedging on the older side in free agency. So, it's kind of neat to juxtapose that with at least at the top of the draft a younger group there where you have a little bit of both as the newcomers on this team. Yeah, I think in all those situations, I I mean, it's great now like um you know, but it wasn't like something we were trying to do in free agency. It wasn't something that we had to do during the draft, you know, it really is kind of like the best player, but I think the veterans coming in that have played a lot of winning football, that have been in big playoff games, having that come in, and then kind of molding these younger guys with what we've had in this building, and then with some guys that have played in big games is going to be a cool mix for us. Can you kind of sum up the emotions from the three days, just kind of Friday what the emotions were, then after day two and getting the Trotter and Tampa first, and then today adding these players? What was each emotion like throughout both of the Each emotion? That's a deep question. Um Well, uttering what or reiterating what Jason said the other day, like I've never seen the draft room so excited when we got Payne. Um our scouting staff erupted from the back room. We I was like, "Where are they? Are they out there?" And they were all the way down the hall, and and we could hear them all. So, really cool clip of them coming in, and just that was exciting. That was awesome. Um Uh not a lot of sleep for me last few days. So, how I felt after all the picks, I'm not I'm pretty even-keeled for the most part, but today is definitely my favorite day. Um I love all the opportunities for us to add really good players at all these levels, and I get jacked about free agency. Most guys upstairs are like, "I can't wait to get this over." And I'm like, "No, we're going to get, you know, great chance here to to uh get all these guys." So, um and then try to see if Greg can find all the names by the end of the night is uh one of my favorite hobbies. That's right. So, yeah. So, I mean, just I mean, this is so much fun for us just to be able to um see the fruits of our labor kind of bear out throughout all these rounds, and um yeah, no, it's just it's so much fun for us. It's what we love to do. So, with some of your picks, uh Trotter, Hurst, they play a position, but within the position there are special designations. So, linebacker you have Mike and Will, wide receiver you have X and Z and that. At what point does their positional uh where they would normally fit within that position play into the evaluation versus maybe another player who plays the overarching uh position, but maybe not that role? Yeah, I would say it's probably twofold. Like when you're evaluating the player, it may not come into your actual grade, your actual eval. You're grading them for what you think they can be. If you're trying to differentiate as far as like the value of like the X versus the F or the Z for the receivers, it kind of comes into play like, "How are we going to use that guy?" For a guy like Ted, um you know, we see him more as a outside receiver, but it's hard to say like I think with the offense now, I don't know that we're going to have a true X. You look at some of the history of of this type of offense now we got with Zach, like I don't know if if there's a pure X. So, obviously without, you know, Mike being here, like those guys are really hard to find. So, if you have that guy, it's awesome, but if you don't, I think we got a really cool group of guys. We got some big guys, we got some little guys, we got a bunch of guys that can run routes, and guys that can block. So, I think that's going to come into play for him. >> And then the linebacker stuff has kind of evolved over the years. I think you really got to be able to play they're really almost interchangeable now. You know, we've talked a lot about, you know, the Mike versus the Mo, and really they've they've become a lot of one in the same. Um just depends now on like the passing game, like how you're going to use Trotter versus Angelone versus Roseboom and Bossick. How are you going to use those guys? Like you're going to try to protect certain guys? Are you going to, you know, enhance what they do well? Um and let those guys kind of do what they do best. So, that may be more in like the actual calls and stuff, but that's more of a probably a Todd question on how he's going to do that, but we're excited to, you know, be able to work with those guys. Just part of the thought process with Trotter, maybe just a byproduct, but with with the league, you know, the offense is always trying to stay ahead of the defense, etc., and a couple years ago it was more spread out, right? And you had lighter and lighter linebackers >> Yep. cover. And now with more 12 and 13 personnel, and the running backs have had a little bit of a resurgence here, a renaissance, is that is that more of the thinking to get a bigger 240-lb linebacker that can play a little bit more downhill to at least stay ahead of the curve, or maybe at the curve? Um I think if they're I mean, we always joke like every time we you get with the coaching staff, it's always like, "We want the big, athletic, fast, tough guy." So, I think the emphasis is always on that. And you know, we've made it known that like emphasis was to get bigger, um which, you know, we're not opposed to taking smaller guys. We've obviously had great success with uh some more undersized guys on our defense in the past, but if we think they're able to do all that and they are big, but yeah, I mean there's what nine tight ends that went in the first 2 days I think which was a record, so you're seeing a lot of more 12 and more 13 personnel. Um, but really like you got to be able to play on all three downs and we think those guys can do that regardless of size, but it's definitely added bonus when you can be a little bigger. Robert, at the start of the day today, back to Keionte, I just want to ask you about uh the nickel as an attack piece and what he does specifically in this defense that that suits him well. >> Yeah, I think it shows up you know when we talk about teams we're getting ready for throughout the season, um you know you got all the different variations of nickel, all the different styles and we've obviously been through a lot of nickels here. Um but like for him like he is really really good going forward, going downhill, attacking line of scrimmage, so blitzing, fitting the run, um being able to get bigger running backs on the ground. And then his ability to just kind of defend the perimeter screen game is really good, so he's really disruptive out there. But he was an outside corner at Auburn, so I think there is the ability for him to be able to run cover um and do all that stuff, but I think just to accentuate what he does best, the thing that stands out to me is just the energy that he plays with. All the TFLs, all the sacks, all the pressures. Were you guys a little surprised that he was available there for you guys in the fourth round? Uh I don't know. I mean we're excited. Um so I mean very happy he was there. It's it's always tough to know who's like you always kind of have a feel who you think's going to go where and then there's always a few surprises, but it's it's it's hard to deal in all the hypotheticals of who you think's going to be there, so I know it's probably sounds like cliche, but kind of just stack it and you know if he's a top guy and he fits us then you just pull the name off. How does that play into who you're looking for as a locker room presence and specifically for the offensive line? Sure, I think offensive line is probably the biggest thing. Um and those are the kind of things that definitely stand out. The way he plays too even character aside, like the way he plays is is is is is is what we desire to be. Um you know and the character backs it up as a captain at Notre Dame. He's got the versatility. So he's just he's got the versatility at both guard spots. Do you envision him learning that center spot as well for you? Uh we'll see. Um I think first and foremost guard, but you know it's always something that I know Carbs and those guys are going to want him to work on eventually, so you know I don't know if it when it clicks, if it clicks, but definitely something we would consider. What are some of the things that you really liked about him enough to want to trade up and get him? Sure. Who else we got with that seventh round pick? Um really excited about Bauer. We're like, ah we're not doing this, so no I'll I'll definitely all in good fun and you know hope those guys nail their draft, so. So with these rookies, with a lot of new free agents, it's going to it might take some time for this unit to kind of gel and all that. That's probably the quickest way to earn the trust and respect your teammates and >> I think guys like Anzalone and A'Shawn on defense as we've as we've talked about a bunch are going to make sure that standard is up there and obviously we got a pretty high one already from from all of our current guys, so excited to see those guys kind of fit in and you know I think they're going to add energy and add juice to that defense too, so I think it can take us to the next level. I mean you guys essentially were done with your draft with 70 picks left. Um did you is that something you could appreciate in terms of the overall depth of the draft? I think it's just something that like we were excited about being able to do and making it something that we wanted to do. I don't really have like specific, you know I don't think we weren't small like you know it wasn't you know something that it was just like a desire to be you know bigger on defense. Um however, I know he played nose quite a bit at Clemson and he even told us he enjoys playing nose. Um I don't know if moving him farther away from the ball is going to accentuate. I think there's stuff we can do with him to help him. Um but I think one-on-ones that his ability to have power and just have pure knockback was you know one of the better ones in the draft, so I think accentuating that and kind of giving him some options to work off of that is going to is going to help.
